Girīśa too, seeing that then, said, "What has happened?"
And Girijā then replied with a laugh to Śambhu:

4.28.s:
girijovāca |
sacchiṣyasya phalaṃ jātaṃ samyagjātaṃ tu śiṣyataḥ |
śāntātmane suvīrāya dattaṃ yadatulaṃ balam ||
4.28.d:
गिरिजोवाच ।
सच्छिष्यस्य फलं जातं सम्यग्जातं तु शिष्यतः ।
शान्तात्मने सुवीराय दत्तं यदतुलं बलम् ॥
4.28.m:
Girijā said:
"The fruit of your good disciple has arisen; indeed, it has arisen fittingly from the disciple,
to whom, a tranquil soul and great hero, matchless strength was granted!"

4.28.s:
sūta uvāca |
girijāyāśca sākūtaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā maheśvaraḥ |
kṛtaghnaṃ rāvaṇaṃ matvā śaśāpa baladarpitam ||
mahādeva uvāca |
re re rāvaṇa durbhakta mā garvaṃ vaha durmate |
śīghraṃ ca tava hastānāṃ darpaghnaśca bhavediha ||
4.28.d:
सूत उवाच ।
गिरिजायाश्च साकूतं वचः श्रुत्वा महेश्वरः ।
कृतघ्नं रावणं मत्वा शशाप बलदर्पितम् ॥
महादेव उवाच ।
रे रे रावण दुर्भक्त मा गर्वं वह दुर्मते ।
शीघ्रं च तव हस्तानां दर्पघ्नश्च भवेदिह ॥
4.28.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard Girijā's sarcastic remark, Maheśvara,
considering Rāvaṇa ungrateful, cursed him who was arrogant with strength:

Mahādeva said:
"O Rāvaṇa, wicked devotee! Do not bear pride, evil-minded one!
Soon a crusher of the pride of your arms shall arise here!"

4.28.s:
sūta uvāva |
iti tatra ca yajjātaṃ nāradaḥ śrutavāṃstadā |
rāvaṇo'pi prasannātmāgātsvadhāma yathāgatam ||
4.28.d:
सूत उवाव ।
इति तत्र च यज्जातं नारदः श्रुतवांस्तदा ।
रावणोऽपि प्रसन्नात्मागात्स्वधाम यथागतम् ॥
4.28.m:
Sūta said:
Then Nārada heard what had happened there.
Rāvaṇa, too, with a delighted mind, went to his own abode just as he had come.

4.28.s:
niścayaṃ paramaṃ kṛtvā balī balavimohitaḥ |
jagadvaśaṃ hi kṛtavān rāvaṇaḥ paradarpahā ||
4.28.d:
निश्चयं परमं कृत्वा बली बलविमोहितः ।
जगद्वशं हि कृतवान् रावणः परदर्पहा ॥
4.28.m:
Having made a firm resolve, that mighty one, deluded by his strength,
Rāvaṇa, the slayer of others' pride, brought the world under his control.

4.28.s:
śivājñayā ca prāptena divyāstreṇa mahaujasā |
rāvaṇasya pratibhaṭo nālaṃ kaścidabhūttadā ||
4.28.d:
शिवाज्ञया च प्राप्तेन दिव्यास्त्रेण महौजसा ।
रावणस्य प्रतिभटो नालं कश्चिदभूत्तदा ॥
4.28.m:
And by means of the divine missile of great splendor obtained by Śiva's command,
no one was able to be a match for Rāvaṇa at that time.

4.28.s:
ityetacca samākhyātaṃ vaidyanātheśvarasya ca |
māhātmyaṃ śṛṇavatāṃ pāpaṃ nṛṇāṃ bhavati bhasmasāt ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
caturthī koṭirudrasaṃhitā
4.28.d:
इत्येतच्च समाख्यातं वैद्यनाथेश्वरस्य च ।
माहात्म्यं शृणवतां पापं नृणां भवति भस्मसात् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
चतुर्थी कोटिरुद्रसंहिता

4.29.s:
sūta uvāca |
athātaḥ sampravakṣyāmi nāgeśākhyaṃ parātmanaḥ |
jyotīrūpaṃ yathā jātaṃ paramaṃ liṅgamuttamam ||
4.29.d:
सूत उवाच ।
अथातः सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि नागेशाख्यं परात्मनः ।
ज्योतीरूपं यथा जातं परमं लिङ्गमुत्तमम् ॥
4.29.m:
Sūta said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain how the supreme, excellent liṅga of the Supreme Self,
known as Nāgeśa, consisting of light, came to be.

4.29.s:
dārukā rākṣasī kācitpārvatīvaradarpitā |
dārukaśca patistasyā babhūva balavattaraḥ ||
4.29.d:
दारुका राक्षसी काचित्पार्वतीवरदर्पिता ।
दारुकश्च पतिस्तस्या बभूव बलवत्तरः ॥
4.29.m:
There was a certain rākṣasī named Dārukā, arrogant on account of Pārvatī's boon;
and her husband Dāruka was exceedingly powerful.

4.29.s:
bahubhī rākṣasaistatra cakāra kadanaṃ satām |
yajñadhvaṃsaṃ ca lokānāṃ dharmadhvaṃsaṃ tadākarot ||
4.29.d:
बहुभी राक्षसैस्तत्र चकार कदनं सताम् ।
यज्ञध्वंसं च लोकानां धर्मध्वंसं तदाकरोत् ॥
4.29.m:
There, along with many rākṣasas, he wrought the slaughter of the good;
he destroyed sacrifices and then destroyed the righteousness of the people.

4.29.s:
paścime sāgare tasya vanaṃ sarvasamṛddhimat |
yojanānāṃ ṣoḍaśabhirvistṛtaṃ sarvato diśam ||
4.29.d:
पश्चिमे सागरे तस्य वनं सर्वसमृद्धिमत् ।
योजनानां षोडशभिर्विस्तृतं सर्वतो दिशम् ॥
4.29.m:
On the western ocean was his forest, endowed with all prosperity,
extending sixteen yojanas in every direction.

4.29.s:
dārukā svavilāsārthaṃ yatra gacchati tadvanam |
bhūmyā ca tarubhistatra sarvopakaraṇairyutam ||
4.29.d:
दारुका स्वविलासार्थं यत्र गच्छति तद्वनम् ।
भूम्या च तरुभिस्तत्र सर्वोपकरणैर्युतम् ॥
4.29.m:
Wherever Dārukā went for her own pleasure, that forest went [too],
complete with its ground, trees, and all its provisions.

4.29.s:
dārukāyai dadau devī tadvanasyāvalokanam |
prayāti tadvanaṃ sā hi patyā saha yadṛcchayā ||
4.29.d:
दारुकायै ददौ देवी तद्वनस्यावलोकनम् ।
प्रयाति तद्वनं सा हि पत्या सह यदृच्छया ॥
4.29.m:
The goddess gave Dārukā the oversight of that forest;
she would travel with that forest at will along with her husband.

4.29.s:
tatra sthitvā tadā so'pi sarveṣāṃ ca bhayaṃ dadau |
dāruko rākṣasaḥ patnyā tayā dārukayā saha ||
4.29.d:
तत्र स्थित्वा तदा सोऽपि सर्वेषां च भयं ददौ ।
दारुको राक्षसः पत्न्या तया दारुकया सह ॥
4.29.m:
Staying there at that time, he also inflicted terror on everyone—
that rākṣasa Dāruka, together with that wife of his, Dārukā.

4.29.s:
te sarve pīḍitā lokā aurvasya śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ |
natvā prītyā viśeṣeṇa tamūcurnatamastakāḥ ||
4.29.d:
ते सर्वे पीडिता लोका और्वस्य शरणं ययुः ।
नत्वा प्रीत्या विशेषेण तमूचुर्नतमस्तकाः ॥
4.29.m:
All those afflicted people went to Aurva for refuge;
bowing with great devotion, with lowered heads, they said to him:

4.29.s:
lokā ūcuḥ |
maharṣe śaraṇaṃ dehi no cedduṣṭaiśca māritāḥ |
sarvaṃ kartuṃ samartho'si tejasā dīptimānasi ||
4.29.d:
लोका ऊचुः ।
महर्षे शरणं देहि नो चेद्दुष्टैश्च मारिताः ।
सर्वं कर्तुं समर्थोऽसि तेजसा दीप्तिमानसि ॥
4.29.m:
The people said:
"O great sage, grant us refuge, or else we are killed by the wicked ones!
You are capable of doing everything; you are radiant with splendor.

4.29.s:
pṛthvyāṃ na vartate kaścittvāṃ vinā śaraṇaṃ ca naḥ |
yāmo yasya samīpe tu sthitvā sukhamavāpnumaḥ ||
4.29.d:
पृथ्व्यां न वर्तते कश्चित्त्वां विना शरणं च नः ।
यामो यस्य समीपे तु स्थित्वा सुखमवाप्नुमः ॥
4.29.m:
On earth there is no one else besides you as our refuge,
approaching whom and staying [near him] we might find peace.

4.29.s:
tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasāḥ sarve palāyante vidūrataḥ |
tvayi śaivaṃ sadā tejo vibhāti jvalano yathā ||
4.29.d:
त्वां दृष्ट्वा राक्षसाः सर्वे पलायन्ते विदूरतः ।
त्वयि शैवं सदा तेजो विभाति ज्वलनो यथा ॥
4.29.m:
Seeing you, all the rākṣasas flee far away;
in you, Śaiva splendor ever shines like fire."

4.29.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityevaṃ prārthito lokairaurvo hi munisattamaḥ |
śocamānaḥ śaraṇyaśca rakṣāyai hi vaco'bravīt ||
4.29.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्येवं प्रार्थितो लोकैरौर्वो हि मुनिसत्तमः ।
शोचमानः शरण्यश्च रक्षायै हि वचोऽब्रवीत् ॥
4.29.m:
Sūta said:
Being thus implored by the people, Aurva, the best of sages,
grieving and being a protector, spoke words for [their] protection:

4.29.s:
aurva uvāca |
pṛthivyāṃ yadi rakṣāṃsi hiṃsyurvai prāṇinastadā |
svayaṃ prāṇairviyujyeyū rākṣasā balavattarāḥ ||
4.29.d:
और्व उवाच ।
पृथिव्यां यदि रक्षांसि हिंस्युर्वै प्राणिनस्तदा ।
स्वयं प्राणैर्वियुज्येयू राक्षसा बलवत्तराः ॥
4.29.m:
Aurva said:
"If the rākṣasas injure living beings on the earth,
then those exceedingly strong rākṣasas shall themselves be deprived of their lives.

4.29.s:
yadā yajñāśca hanyeraṃstadā prāṇairviyojitāḥ |
bhavantu rākṣasāḥ sarve satyametanmayocyate ||
4.29.d:
यदा यज्ञाश्च हन्येरंस्तदा प्राणैर्वियोजिताः ।
भवन्तु राक्षसाः सर्वे सत्यमेतन्मयोच्यते ॥
4.29.m:
Whenever sacrifices are destroyed, let all the rākṣasas
be deprived of their lives; this that I speak is the truth."

4.29.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityuktvā vacanaṃ tebhyaḥ samāśvāsya prajāḥ punaḥ |
tapaścakāra vividhamaurvo lokasukhāvahaḥ ||
4.29.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा वचनं तेभ्यः समाश्वास्य प्रजाः पुनः ।
तपश्चकार विविधमौर्वो लोकसुखावहः ॥
4.29.m:
Sūta said:
Having spoken these words to them and reassured the subjects,
Aurva, who brings happiness to the world, performed various austerities.

4.29.s:
devāstadā te vijñāya śāpasya kāraṇaṃ hi tat |
yuddhāya ca samudyogaṃ cakrurdevāribhiḥ saha ||
4.29.d:
देवास्तदा ते विज्ञाय शापस्य कारणं हि तत् ।
युद्धाय च समुद्योगं चक्रुर्देवारिभिः सह ॥
4.29.m:
The gods, learning then of the cause of that curse,
made preparation for battle with the enemies of the gods.

4.29.s:
sarvaiścaiva prayatnaiśca nānāyudhadharāḥ surāḥ |
sarve śakrādayastatra yuddhārthaṃ samupāgatāḥ ||
4.29.d:
सर्वैश्चैव प्रयत्नैश्च नानायुधधराः सुराः ।
सर्वे शक्रादयस्तत्र युद्धार्थं समुपागताः ॥
4.29.m:
With all efforts, the gods, bearing various weapons,
all of them, Śakra and the others, arrived there for battle.

4.29.s:
tāndṛṣṭvā rākṣasāstatra vicāre tatparāḥ punaḥ |
babhūvuste'khilā duṣṭā mitho ye yatra saṃsthitāḥ ||
4.29.d:
तान्दृष्ट्वा राक्षसास्तत्र विचारे तत्पराः पुनः ।
बभूवुस्तेऽखिला दुष्टा मिथो ये यत्र संस्थिताः ॥
4.29.m:
Seeing them, the rākṣasas there then engaged in deliberation—
all those wicked ones who were assembled there with one another.

4.29.s:
rākṣasā ūcuḥ |
kiṃ kartavyaṃ kva gantavyaṃ saṅkaṭaṃ samupāgatāḥ |
yuddhyate mriyate caiva yuddhyate na vihanyate ||
4.29.d:
राक्षसा ऊचुः ।
किं कर्तव्यं क्व गन्तव्यं सङ्कटं समुपागताः ।
युद्ध्यते म्रियते चैव युद्ध्यते न विहन्यते ॥
4.29.m:
The rākṣasas said:
"What is to be done? Where should we go? We have fallen into danger:
if one fights, one dies; if one does not fight, one is still struck down.

4.29.s:
tathaiva sthīyate cedvai bhakṣyate kiṃ parasparam |
duḥkhaṃ hi sarvathā jātaṃ ka enaṃ vinivārayet ||
4.29.d:
तथैव स्थीयते चेद्वै भक्ष्यते किं परस्परम् ।
दुःखं हि सर्वथा जातं क एनं विनिवारयेत् ॥
4.29.m:
If we simply stay like this, shall we eat one another?
Misery has indeed arisen in every way; who can avert this?"

4.29.s:
sūta uvāca |
vicāryeti ca te tatra dārukādyāśca rākṣasāḥ |
upāyaṃ na vijānanto duḥkhaṃ prāptāḥ sadā hi vai ||
4.29.d:
सूत उवाच ।
विचार्येति च ते तत्र दारुकाद्याश्च राक्षसाः ।
उपायं न विजानन्तो दुःखं प्राप्ताः सदा हि वै ॥
4.29.m:
Sūta said:
Deliberating thus, those rākṣasas, Dārukā and the others,
not knowing any remedy, constantly experienced misery.

4.29.s:
dārukā rākṣasī cāpi jñātvā duḥkhaṃ samāgatam |
bhavānyāśca varaṃ taṃ ca kathayāmāsa sā tadā ||
4.29.d:
दारुका राक्षसी चापि ज्ञात्वा दुःखं समागतम् ।
भवान्याश्च वरं तं च कथयामास सा तदा ॥
4.29.m:
And the rākṣasī Dārukā, seeing the misery that had arrived,
then spoke of that boon from Bhavānī:

4.29.s:
dārukovāca |
mayā hyārādhitā pūrvaṃ bhavapatnī varaṃ dadau |
vanaṃ gaccha nijaiḥ sārdhaṃ yatra gantuṃ tvamicchasi ||
4.29.d:
दारुकोवाच ।
मया ह्याराधिता पूर्वं भवपत्नी वरं ददौ ।
वनं गच्छ निजैः सार्धं यत्र गन्तुं त्वमिच्छसि ॥
4.29.m:
Dārukā said:
"The wife of Bhava was propitiated by me formerly, and she granted a boon:
'Go with your own people with the forest wherever you wish to go.'

4.29.s:
tadvaraśca mayā prāptaḥ kathaṃ duḥkhaṃ viṣahyate |
jale vanaṃ ca nītvā vai sukhaṃ stheyaṃ tu rākṣasaiḥ ||
4.29.d:
तद्वरश्च मया प्राप्तः कथं दुःखं विषह्यते ।
जले वनं च नीत्वा वै सुखं स्थेयं तु राक्षसैः ॥
4.29.m:
That boon was obtained by me; why should misery be endured?
Taking the forest into the water, let the rākṣasas live in comfort."

4.29.s:
sūta uvāca |
tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasyā harṣamāgatāḥ |
ūcuḥ sarve mithaste hi rākṣasā nirbhayāstadā ||
4.29.d:
सूत उवाच ।
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्या हर्षमागताः ।
ऊचुः सर्वे मिथस्ते हि राक्षसा निर्भयास्तदा ॥

4.29.s:
dhanyeyaṃ kṛtakṛtyeyaṃ rājñyā vai jīvitāḥ svayam |
natvā tasyai ca tatsarvaṃ kathayāmāsurādarāt ||
4.29.d:
धन्येयं कृतकृत्येयं राज्ञ्या वै जीविताः स्वयम् ।
नत्वा तस्यै च तत्सर्वं कथयामासुरादरात् ॥
4.29.m:
"Blessed is she! Accomplished in her aim is she! We have been saved by the queen herself!"
And bowing to her, they said all this with respect:

4.29.s:
yadi gantuṃ bhavecchaktirgamyatāṃ kiṃ vicāryate |
tatra gatvā jale devi sukhaṃ sthāsyāma nityaśaḥ ||
4.29.d:
यदि गन्तुं भवेच्छक्तिर्गम्यतां किं विचार्यते ।
तत्र गत्वा जले देवि सुखं स्थास्याम नित्यशः ॥
4.29.m:
"If there is the power to go, let us go! Why hesitate?
Having gone there into the water, O goddess, we shall live in comfort perpetually."

4.29.s:
etasminnantare lokā devaiḥ sārdhaṃ samāgatāḥ |
yuddhāya vividhairduḥkhaiḥ pīḍitā rākṣasaiḥ purā ||
4.29.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे लोका देवैः सार्धं समागताः ।
युद्धाय विविधैर्दुःखैः पीडिता राक्षसैः पुरा ॥
4.29.m:
In the meantime, the people arrived along with the gods
for battle, having formerly been tormented with diverse miseries by the rākṣasas.

4.29.s:
pīḍitāśca tadā tasyā bhavānyā balamāśritāḥ |
samagraṃ nagaraṃ nītvā jalasthalasamanvitam ||
4.29.d:
पीडिताश्च तदा तस्या भवान्या बलमाश्रिताः ।
समग्रं नगरं नीत्वा जलस्थलसमन्वितम् ॥
4.29.m:
And then, hard-pressed, relying on the power of that Bhavānī,
she took the entire city along with its water and land,

4.29.s:
jaya jayeti devyāstu stutimuccārya rākṣasī |
tata uḍḍīyanaṃ kṛtvā sapakṣo girirāḍyathā ||
4.29.d:
जय जयेति देव्यास्तु स्तुतिमुच्चार्य राक्षसी ।
तत उड्डीयनं कृत्वा सपक्षो गिरिराड्यथा ॥
4.29.m:
and uttering the praise of the goddess, "Victory! Victory!", the rākṣasī
then flew up like a winged king of mountains;

4.29.s:
samudrasya ca madhye sā saṃsthitā nirbhayā tadā |
sakalaiḥ parivāraiśca mumudeti śivānugā ||
4.29.d:
समुद्रस्य च मध्ये सा संस्थिता निर्भया तदा ।
सकलैः परिवारैश्च मुमुदेति शिवानुगा ॥
4.29.m:
and situated in the midst of the ocean, fearless then,
together with her entire retinue, that follower of Śiva rejoiced.

4.29.s:
tatra sindhau ca te sthitvā nagare ca vilāsinaḥ |
rākṣasāśca sukhaṃ prāpurnirbhayāśca vijahrire ||
4.29.d:
तत्र सिन्धौ च ते स्थित्वा नगरे च विलासिनः ।
राक्षसाश्च सुखं प्रापुर्निर्भयाश्च विजह्रिरे ॥
4.29.m: Dwelling there in the sea and in the city, those pleasure-seeking / rākṣasas attained happiness and disported without fear.

4.29.s:
rākṣasāśca pṛthivyāṃ vai nājagmuśca kadācana |
muneḥ śāpabhayādeva babhramuste cale tadā ||
4.29.d:
राक्षसाश्च पृथिव्यां वै नाजग्मुश्च कदाचन ।
मुनेः शापभयादेव बभ्रमुस्ते चले तदा ॥
4.29.m: The rākṣasas never went onto the land; / out of fear of the sage's curse, they then wandered in the water.

4.29.s:
nauṣu sthitān janānnītvā nagare tatra tāṃstadā |
cikṣipurbandhanāgāre kāṃścijjaghnustadā hi te ||
4.29.d:
नौषु स्थितान् जनान्नीत्वा नगरे तत्र तांस्तदा ।
चिक्षिपुर्बन्धनागारे कांश्चिज्जघ्नुस्तदा हि ते ॥
4.29.m: Seizing the people aboard boats, they brought them to that city, / threw them into prison, and then killed some [of them].

4.29.s:
yathā yathā punaḥ pīḍāṃ cakruste rākṣasāstadā |
tatra sthitā bhavānyāśca varadānācca nirbhayāḥ ||
4.29.d:
यथा यथा पुनः पीडां चक्रुस्ते राक्षसास्तदा ।
तत्र स्थिता भवान्याश्च वरदानाच्च निर्भयाः ॥
4.29.m: Thus the rākṣasas, residing there, caused affliction repeatedly, / fearless by the boon granted by Bhavānī.

4.29.s:
yathā pūrvaṃ sthale loke bhayaṃ cāsīnnirantaram |
tathā bhayaṃ jale teṣāmāsīnnityaṃ munīśvarāḥ ||
4.29.d:
यथा पूर्वं स्थले लोके भयं चासीन्निरन्तरम् ।
तथा भयं जले तेषामासीन्नित्यं मुनीश्वराः ॥
4.29.m: Just as formerly there was constant fear among people on land, / so was there always fear for them on the water, O best of sages.

4.29.s:
kadācidrākṣasī sā ca niḥsṛtā nagarājjale |
ruddhvā mārgaṃ sthitā lokapīḍārthaṃ dharaṇau ca hi ||
4.29.d:
कदाचिद्राक्षसी सा च निःसृता नगराज्जले ।
रुद्ध्वा मार्गं स्थिता लोकपीडार्थं धरणौ च हि ॥
4.29.m: Once that rākṣasī emerged from the city onto the water / and stood blocking the path on earth to torment people.

4.29.s:
etasminnantare tatra nāvo bahutarāḥ śubhāḥ |
āgatā bahudhā tatra sarvato lokasaṃvṛtāḥ ||
4.29.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र नावो बहुतराः शुभाः ।
आगता बहुधा तत्र सर्वतो लोकसंवृताः ॥
4.29.m: Meanwhile, numerous splendid boats arrived there, / filled from all sides with people coming in various directions.

4.29.s:
tā nāvaśca tadā dṛṣṭvā harṣaṃ samprāpya rākṣasāḥ |
drutaṃ gatvā hi tatrasthānvegātsandadhrire khalāḥ ||
4.29.d:
ता नावश्च तदा दृष्ट्वा हर्षं सम्प्राप्य राक्षसाः ।
द्रुतं गत्वा हि तत्रस्थान्वेगात्सन्दध्रिरे खलाः ॥
4.29.m: Seeing those boats, the rākṣasas were filled with joy; / those villains went swiftly and seized the people aboard with speed.

4.29.s:
ājagmurnagaraṃ te ca tānādāya mahābalāḥ |
cikṣipurbandhanāgāre baddhvā hi nigaḍairdṛḍhaiḥ ||
4.29.d:
आजग्मुर्नगरं ते च तानादाय महाबलाः ।
चिक्षिपुर्बन्धनागारे बद्ध्वा हि निगडैर्दृढैः ॥
4.29.m: Taking them, those powerful [demons] returned to the city / and threw them into prison, having bound them with strong chains.

4.29.s:
baddhāste nigaḍairlokāḥ saṃsthitā bandhanālaye |
atīva duḥkhamājagmurbhartsitāste muhurmuhuḥ ||
4.29.d:
बद्धास्ते निगडैर्लोकाः संस्थिता बन्धनालये ।
अतीव दुःखमाजग्मुर्भर्त्सितास्ते मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
4.29.m: Bound with chains and confined in the prison-house, / those people suffered extreme grief, being scolded again and again.

4.29.s:
teṣāṃ madhye ca yo'dhīśaḥ sa vaiśyaḥ supriyābhidhaḥ |
śivapriyaḥ śubhācāraḥ śaivaścāsītsadātanaḥ ||
4.29.d:
तेषां मध्ये च योऽधीशः स वैश्यः सुप्रियाभिधः ।
शिवप्रियः शुभाचारः शैवश्चासीत्सदातनः ॥
4.29.m: Among them was a leader, a vaiśya named Supriya, / beloved of Śiva, of good conduct, and an eternal Śaiva devotee.

4.29.s:
vinā ca śivapūjāṃ vai na tiṣṭhati kadācana |
sarvathā śivadharmā hi bhasmarudrākṣabhūṣaṇaḥ ||
4.29.d:
विना च शिवपूजां वै न तिष्ठति कदाचन ।
सर्वथा शिवधर्मा हि भस्मरुद्राक्षभूषणः ॥
4.29.m: He never stayed without performing worship to Śiva; / he adhered entirely to the Śaiva way, adorned with ashes and rudrākṣas.

4.29.s:
yadi pūjā na jātā cenna bhunakti tadā tu saḥ |
atastatrāpi vaiśyo'sau cakāra śivapūjanam ||
4.29.d:
यदि पूजा न जाता चेन्न भुनक्ति तदा तु सः ।
अतस्तत्रापि वैश्योऽसौ चकार शिवपूजनम् ॥
4.29.m: If worship was not performed, he would not eat. / Therefore, even there, that vaiśya performed worship to Śiva.

4.29.s:
kārāgṛhagataḥ so'pi bahūṃścāśikṣayattadā |
śivamantraṃ ca pūjāṃ ca pārthivīmṛṣisattamāḥ ||
4.29.d:
कारागृहगतः सोऽपि बहूंश्चाशिक्षयत्तदा ।
शिवमन्त्रं च पूजां च पार्थिवीमृषिसत्तमाः ॥
4.29.m: Though confined in prison, he taught many others / the mantra of Śiva and the worship of earthen [liṅgas], O best of sages.

4.29.s:
te sarve ca tadā tatra śivapūjāṃ svakāmadām |
cakrire vidhivattatra yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam ||
4.29.d:
ते सर्वे च तदा तत्र शिवपूजां स्वकामदाम् ।
चक्रिरे विधिवत्तत्र यथादृष्टं यथाश्रुतम् ॥
4.29.m: All of them then performed worship to Śiva there to fulfill their desires, / according to the rules, as they had seen and heard.

4.29.s:
kecittatra sthitā dhyāne baddhvāsanamanuttamam |
mānasīṃ śivapūjāṃ ca keciccakrurmudānvitāḥ ||
4.29.d:
केचित्तत्र स्थिता ध्याने बद्ध्वासनमनुत्तमम् ।
मानसीं शिवपूजां च केचिच्चक्रुर्मुदान्विताः ॥
4.29.m: Some sat there in meditation, having assumed an excellent posture; / others, filled with joy, performed mental worship to Śiva.

4.29.s:
tadādhīśena tatraiva pratyakṣaṃ śivapūjanam |
kṛtaṃ ca pārthivasyaiva vidhānena munīśvarāḥ ||
4.29.d:
तदाधीशेन तत्रैव प्रत्यक्षं शिवपूजनम् ।
कृतं च पार्थिवस्यैव विधानेन मुनीश्वराः ॥
4.29.m: By their leader himself, direct worship of Śiva / was performed there according to the rites of the earthen [liṅga], O best of sages.

4.29.s:
anye ca ye na jānanti vidhānaṃ smaraṇaṃ param |
namaḥ śivāya mantreṇa dhyāyantaḥ śaṅkaraṃ sthitāḥ ||
4.29.d:
अन्ये च ये न जानन्ति विधानं स्मरणं परम् ।
नमः शिवाय मन्त्रेण ध्यायन्तः शङ्करं स्थिताः ॥
4.29.m: Others who did not know the ritual method stood absorbed in supreme remembrance, / meditating on Śaṅkara with the mantra 'namaḥ śivāya'.

4.29.s:
supriyo nāma yaścāsīdvaiśyavaryaḥ śivapriyaḥ |
dhyāyam̐śca manasā tatra cakāra śivapūjanam ||
4.29.d:
सुप्रियो नाम यश्चासीद्वैश्यवर्यः शिवप्रियः ।
ध्यायम्̐श्च मनसा तत्र चकार शिवपूजनम् ॥
4.29.m: He who was named Supriya, the foremost of vaiśyas and beloved of Śiva, / meditated in his mind and performed worship to Śiva there.

4.29.s:
yathoktarūpī śambhuśca pratyakṣaṃ sarvamādade |
so'pi svayaṃ na jānāti gṛhyate na śivena vai ||
4.29.d:
यथोक्तरूपी शम्भुश्च प्रत्यक्षं सर्वमाददे ।
सोऽपि स्वयं न जानाति गृह्यते न शिवेन वै ॥
4.29.m: And Śambhu, assuming the form described, directly received everything; / he himself did not even know that it was being received by Śiva.

4.29.s:
evaṃ ca kriyamāṇasya vaiśyasya śivapūjanam |
vyatīyustatra ṣaṇmāsā nirvighnena munīśvarāḥ ||
4.29.d:
एवं च क्रियमाणस्य वैश्यस्य शिवपूजनम् ।
व्यतीयुस्तत्र षण्मासा निर्विघ्नेन मुनीश्वराः ॥
4.29.m: While the vaiśya was thus performing the worship of Śiva, / six months passed there without obstacle, O best of sages.

4.29.s:
ataḥ paraṃ ca yajjātaṃ caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ |
tacchṛṇudhvamṛṣiśreṣṭhāḥ sāvadhānena cetasā ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
caturthī koṭirudrasaṃhitā
4.29.d:
अतः परं च यज्जातं चरितं शशिमौलिनः ।
तच्छृणुध्वमृषिश्रेष्ठाः सावधानेन चेतसा ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
चतुर्थी कोटिरुद्रसंहिता
4.29.m:
Listen with attentive mind, O best of sages, / to the deed of the moon-crested [Lord] that took place after this.

Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, titled 'Description of the Affliction Caused by the Rākṣasas of Dārukāvana' in the Nāgeśvara-jyotirliṅga-māhātmya of the Koṭirudrasaṃhitā, the fourth [section] of the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

4.30.s:
sūta uvāca |
kadācitsevakastasya rākṣasasya durātmanaḥ |
tadagre sundaraṃ rūpaṃ śaṅkarasya dadarśa ha ||
4.30.d:
सूत उवाच ।
कदाचित्सेवकस्तस्य राक्षसस्य दुरात्मनः ।
तदग्रे सुन्दरं रूपं शङ्करस्य ददर्श ह ॥
4.30.m: Sūta said: / Once, a servant of that wicked rākṣasa / beheld the handsome form of Śaṅkara before him.

4.30.s:
tasmai niveditaṃ rājñe rākṣasānāṃ yathārthakam |
sarvaṃ taccaritaṃ tena sakautukamathādbhutam ||
4.30.d:
तस्मै निवेदितं राज्ञे राक्षसानां यथार्थकम् ।
सर्वं तच्चरितं तेन सकौतुकमथाद्भुतम् ॥
4.30.m: He truthfully reported to that king of rākṣasas / all of that extraordinary and wonderful occurrence.

4.30.s:
rājāpi tatra cāgatya rākṣasānāṃ sa dārukaḥ |
vihvalaḥ sabalaḥ śīghraṃ paryapṛcchacca taṃ śivam ||
4.30.d:
राजापि तत्र चागत्य राक्षसानां स दारुकः ।
विह्वलः सबलः शीघ्रं पर्यपृच्छच्च तं शिवम् ॥
4.30.m: That king of the rākṣasas, Dāruka, also came there, / perturbed and accompanied by his forces, and quickly questioned that devotee of Śiva:

4.30.s:
dāruka uvāca |
kiṃ dhyāyasi hi vaiśya tvaṃ satyaṃ vada mamāgrataḥ |
evaṃ sati na mṛtyuste mama vākyaṃ ca nānyathā ||
4.30.d:
दारुक उवाच ।
किं ध्यायसि हि वैश्य त्वं सत्यं वद ममाग्रतः ।
एवं सति न मृत्युस्ते मम वाक्यं च नान्यथा ॥
4.30.m: Dāruka said: / 'O vaiśya, what are you meditating upon? Tell the truth before me! / If you do, there will be no death for you; my word is never otherwise.'

4.30.s:
sūta uvāca |
tenoktaṃ ca na jānāmi tacchrutvā kupitaḥ sa vai |
rākṣasānprerayāmāsa hanyatāṃ rākṣasā ayam ||
4.30.d:
सूत उवाच ।
तेनोक्तं च न जानामि तच्छ्रुत्वा कुपितः स वै ।
राक्षसान्प्रेरयामास हन्यतां राक्षसा अयम् ॥
4.30.m: Sūta said: / He replied, 'I do not know.' Hearing that, [Dāruka] was enraged, / and commanded the rākṣasas: 'Let this man be killed, O rākṣasas!'

4.30.s:
taduktāste tadā hantuṃ nānāyudhadharā gatāḥ |
drutaṃ taṃ vaiśyaśārdūlaṃ śaṅkarāsaktacetasam ||
4.30.d:
तदुक्तास्ते तदा हन्तुं नानायुधधरा गताः ।
द्रुतं तं वैश्यशार्दूलं शङ्करासक्तचेतसम् ॥
4.30.m: Commanded by him, they, bearing various weapons, quickly set out to kill / that tiger among vaiśyas whose mind was fixed on Śaṅkara.

4.30.s:
tānāgatāṃstadā dṛṣṭvā bhayavitrastalocanaḥ |
śivaṃ sasmāra suprītyā tannāmāni jagau muhuḥ ||
4.30.d:
तानागतांस्तदा दृष्ट्वा भयवित्रस्तलोचनः ।
शिवं सस्मार सुप्रीत्या तन्नामानि जगौ मुहुः ॥
4.30.m: Seeing them coming, his eyes trembling with fear, / he remembered Śiva with deep affection and repeatedly sang his names.

4.30.s:
vaiśyapatiruvāca |
pāhi śaṅkara deveśa pāhi śambho śiveti ca |
duṣṭādasmāttrilokeśa khalahan bhaktavatsala ||
4.30.d:
वैश्यपतिरुवाच ।
पाहि शङ्कर देवेश पाहि शम्भो शिवेति च ।
दुष्टादस्मात्त्रिलोकेश खलहन् भक्तवत्सल ॥
4.30.m: The leader of the vaiśyas said: / 'Protect me, O Śaṅkara, Lord of gods! Protect me, O Śambhu, Śiva! / Deliver me from this wicked villain, O Lord of the three worlds, affectionate toward devotees!

4.30.s:
sarvasvaṃ ca bhavānadya mama deva tvameva hi |
tvadadhīnastvadīyo'haṃ tvatprāṇaḥ sarvadā prabho ||
4.30.d:
सर्वस्वं च भवानद्य मम देव त्वमेव हि ।
त्वदधीनस्त्वदीयोऽहं त्वत्प्राणः सर्वदा प्रभो ॥
4.30.m: You alone are indeed my all today, O Lord! / I am dependent on you, I am yours, and my life belongs to you always, O Master!'

4.30.s:
sūta uvāca |
iti samprārthitaḥ śambhurvivarānnirgatastadā |
bhavanenottamenātha caturdvārayutena ca ||
4.30.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इति सम्प्रार्थितः शम्भुर्विवरान्निर्गतस्तदा ।
भवनेनोत्तमेनाथ चतुर्द्वारयुतेन च ॥
4.30.m: Sūta said: / Being thus prayed to, Śambhu then emerged from a cavity / together with an excellent mansion furnished with four gates.

4.30.s:
madhya jyotiḥsvarūpaṃ ca śivarūpaṃ tadadbhutam |
parivārasamāyuktaṃ dṛṣṭvā cāpūjayatsa vai ||
4.30.d:
मध्य ज्योतिःस्वरूपं च शिवरूपं तदद्भुतम् ।
परिवारसमायुक्तं दृष्ट्वा चापूजयत्स वै ॥
4.30.m: Having beheld that wondrous form of Śiva in the middle, having the nature of light, / accompanied by his attendants, he worshipped him.

4.30.s:
pūjitaśca tadā śambhuḥ prasanno hyabhavatsvayam |
astraṃ pāśupataṃ nāma dattvā rākṣasapuṅgavān ||
4.30.d:
पूजितश्च तदा शम्भुः प्रसन्नो ह्यभवत्स्वयम् ।
अस्त्रं पाशुपतं नाम दत्त्वा राक्षसपुङ्गवान् ॥
4.30.m: And being worshipped, Śambhu was pleased. / Bestowing the weapon named Pāśupata upon the chief of the rākṣasas,

4.30.s:
jaghāna sopakaraṇāṃstānsarvānsagaṇāndrutam |
arakṣacca svabhaktaṃ vai duṣṭahā sa hi śaṅkaraḥ ||
4.30.d:
जघान सोपकरणांस्तान्सर्वान्सगणान्द्रुतम् ।
अरक्षच्च स्वभक्तं वै दुष्टहा स हि शङ्करः ॥
4.30.m: he swiftly struck down all of them with their equipment and their troops; / and that Śaṅkara, the destroyer of the wicked, protected his devotee.

4.30.s:
sarvāṃstāṃśca tadā hatvā varaṃ prādādvanasya ca |
atyadbhutakaraḥ śambhuḥ svalīlāttasuvigrahaḥ ||
4.30.d:
सर्वांस्तांश्च तदा हत्वा वरं प्रादाद्वनस्य च ।
अत्यद्भुतकरः शम्भुः स्वलीलात्तसुविग्रहः ॥
4.30.m: Having slain all of them, Śambhu, who works great wonders / and assumes a beautiful form through his sport, bestowed a boon upon the forest:

4.30.s:
asminvane sadā varṇadharmā vai sambhavantu ca |
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ hi tathaiva ca ||
4.30.d:
अस्मिन्वने सदा वर्णधर्मा वै सम्भवन्तु च ।
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां हि तथैव च ॥
4.30.m: 'In this forest let the duties of the social classes always prevail / for brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and likewise for śūdras.

4.30.s:
bhavantvatra muniśreṣṭhāstāmasā na kadācana |
śivadharmapravaktāraḥ śivadharmapravartakāḥ ||
4.30.d:
भवन्त्वत्र मुनिश्रेष्ठास्तामसा न कदाचन ।
शिवधर्मप्रवक्तारः शिवधर्मप्रवर्तकाः ॥
4.30.m: Let there be the best of sages here, never [people of] tamas; / let them be proclaimers of the Śaiva duties and promoters of the Śaiva duties.'

4.30.s:
sūta uvāca |
etasminsamaye sā vai rākṣasī dārukāhvayā |
devyāḥ stutiṃ cakārāsau pārvatyā dīnamānasā ||
4.30.d:
सूत उवाच ।
एतस्मिन्समये सा वै राक्षसी दारुकाह्वया ।
देव्याः स्तुतिं चकारासौ पार्वत्या दीनमानसा ॥
4.30.m: Sūta said: / At that time, that rākṣasī named Dārukā, / with a distressed mind, offered praise to the goddess Pārvatī.

4.30.s:
prasannā ca tadā devī kiṃ karomītyuvāca hi |
sāpyuvāca punastatra vaṃśo me rakṣyatāṃ tvayā ||
4.30.d:
प्रसन्ना च तदा देवी किं करोमीत्युवाच हि ।
साप्युवाच पुनस्तत्र वंशो मे रक्ष्यतां त्वया ॥
4.30.m: The goddess was pleased and said, 'What shall I do [for you]?' / And she answered there, 'May my lineage be protected by you.'

4.30.s:
rakṣayiṣyāmi te vaṃśaṃ satyaṃ ca kathyate mayā |
ityuktvā ca śivenaiva vigrahaṃ sā cakāra ha ||
4.30.d:
रक्षयिष्यामि ते वंशं सत्यं च कथ्यते मया ।
इत्युक्त्वा च शिवेनैव विग्रहं सा चकार ह ॥
4.30.m: 'I will protect your lineage; what I speak is the truth.' / Having spoken thus, she indeed entered into conflict with Śiva.

4.30.s:
śivo'pi kupitāṃ devīṃ dṛṣṭvā varavaśaḥ prabhuḥ |
pratyuvāceti suprītyā yathecchasi tathā kuru ||
4.30.d:
शिवोऽपि कुपितां देवीं दृष्ट्वा वरवशः प्रभुः ।
प्रत्युवाचेति सुप्रीत्या यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
4.30.m: Śiva too, seeing the goddess angered, being bound by her boon, the Lord / replied with great fondness, 'Do as you wish.'

4.30.s:
sūta uvāca |
iti śrutvā vacastasya svapateḥ śaṅkarasya vai |
suprasannā vihasyāśu pārvatī vākyamabravīt ||
4.30.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य स्वपतेः शङ्करस्य वै ।
सुप्रसन्ना विहस्याशु पार्वती वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
4.30.m: Sūta said: / Hearing this word of her husband Śaṅkara, / Pārvatī, exceedingly pleased, smiled immediately and spoke these words:

4.30.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
bhavadīyaṃ vacastathyaṃ yugānte sambhaviṣyati |
tāvacca tāmasī sṛṣṭirbhavatviti mataṃ mama ||
4.30.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
भवदीयं वचस्तथ्यं युगान्ते सम्भविष्यति ।
तावच्च तामसी सृष्टिर्भवत्विति मतं मम ॥
4.30.m: Pārvatī said: / 'Your statement is true; it will come to pass at the end of the yuga. / Until then, let the tamasic creation exist—this is my opinion.

4.30.s:
anyathā pralayaḥ syādvai satyaṃ me vyāhṛtaṃ śiva |
pramāṇīkriyatāṃ nātha tvadīyāsmi tvadāśrayā ||
4.30.d:
अन्यथा प्रलयः स्याद्वै सत्यं मे व्याहृतं शिव ।
प्रमाणीक्रियतां नाथ त्वदीयास्मि त्वदाश्रया ॥
4.30.m: Otherwise, a dissolution would certainly take place; I have spoken the truth, O Śiva. / Let this be authorized, O Lord; I am yours, having taken refuge in you.

4.30.s:
iyaṃ ca dārukā devī rākṣasī śaktikā mama |
baliṣṭhā rākṣasīnāṃ ca rakṣorājyaṃ praśāstu ca ||
4.30.d:
इयं च दारुका देवी राक्षसी शक्तिका मम ।
बलिष्ठा राक्षसीनां च रक्षोराज्यं प्रशास्तु च ॥
4.30.m: And this goddess Dārukā, a rākṣasī, is my own power. / Strongest among the rākṣasīs, let her rule over the realm of the rākṣasas.

4.30.s:
imā rākṣasapatnyastu prasaviṣyanti putrakān |
te sarve militāścaiva vane vāsāya me matāḥ ||
4.30.d:
इमा राक्षसपत्न्यस्तु प्रसविष्यन्ति पुत्रकान् ।
ते सर्वे मिलिताश्चैव वने वासाय मे मताः ॥
4.30.m: These wives of the rākṣasas shall give birth to sons. / All of them united, in my judgment, shall dwell in the forest.'

4.30.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā pārvatyāḥ svastriyāḥ prabhuḥ |
prasannamānaso bhūtvā śaṅkaro vākyamabravīt ||
4.30.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्येवं वचनं श्रुत्वा पार्वत्याः स्वस्त्रियाः प्रभुः ।
प्रसन्नमानसो भूत्वा शङ्करो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
4.30.m: Sūta said: / Hearing these words of Pārvatī, his wife, the Lord, / Śaṅkara, became pleased at heart and spoke these words:

4.30.s:
śaṅkara uvāca |
iti bravīṣi tvaṃ vai cecchṛṇu madvacanaṃ priye |
sthāsyāmyasminvane prītyā bhaktānāṃ pālanāya ca ||
4.30.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ।
इति ब्रवीषि त्वं वै चेच्छृणु मद्वचनं प्रिये ।
स्थास्याम्यस्मिन्वने प्रीत्या भक्तानां पालनाय च ॥
4.30.m: Śaṅkara said: / If you indeed say so, listen to my words, dear one: / I shall abide in this forest with delight and to protect the devotees.

4.30.s:
atra me varṇadharmastho darśanaṃ prītisaṃyutam |
kariṣyati ca yo vai sa cakravartī bhaviṣyati ||
4.30.d:
अत्र मे वर्णधर्मस्थो दर्शनं प्रीतिसंयुतम् ।
करिष्यति च यो वै स चक्रवर्ती भविष्यति ॥
4.30.m: 'Whoever, established in the duty of the social classes, shall behold me here with love, / he shall indeed become an emperor.

4.30.s:
anyathā kaliparyāye satyasyādau nṛpeśvaraḥ |
mahāsenayuto yo vai vīraseneti viśrutaḥ ||
4.30.d:
अन्यथा कलिपर्याये सत्यस्यादौ नृपेश्वरः ।
महासेनयुतो यो वै वीरसेनेति विश्रुतः ॥
4.30.m: Otherwise, during the course of the Kali[yuga], at the beginning of the Satya[yuga], a king of kings, / accompanied by a vast army, renowned by the name Vīrasena,

4.30.s:
sa me bhaktyātivikrānto darśanaṃ me kariṣyati |
darśanaṃ me sa kṛtvaiva cakravartī bhaviṣyati ||
4.30.d:
स मे भक्त्यातिविक्रान्तो दर्शनं मे करिष्यति ।
दर्शनं मे स कृत्वैव चक्रवर्ती भविष्यति ॥
4.30.m: exceedingly valiant, shall behold me through devotion to me. / Having beheld me, he shall indeed become an emperor.'

4.30.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityevaṃ dampatī tau ca kṛtvā hāsyaṃ parasparam |
sthitau tatra svayaṃ sākṣānmahotīkārakau dvijāḥ ||
4.30.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्येवं दम्पती तौ च कृत्वा हास्यं परस्परम् ।
स्थितौ तत्र स्वयं साक्षान्महोतीकारकौ द्विजाः ॥
4.30.m: Sūta said: / Thus that couple, having shared a smile with each other, / remained there visibly in person, conferring great benefit, O twice-born ones.

4.30.s:
jyotirliṅgasvarūpo hi nāmnā nāgeśvaraḥ śivaḥ |
nāgeśvarī śivā devī babhūva ca satāṃ priyau ||
4.30.d:
ज्योतिर्लिङ्गस्वरूपो हि नाम्ना नागेश्वरः शिवः ।
नागेश्वरी शिवा देवी बभूव च सतां प्रियौ ॥
4.30.m: Śiva in the form of a liṅga of light indeed became Nāgeśvara by name, / and the auspicious goddess became Nāgeśvarī, dear to the virtuous.

4.30.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
vīrasenaḥ kathaṃ tatra yāsyate dārukāvane |
kathamarciṣyati śivaṃ tvaṃ tadvada mahāmate ||
4.30.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
वीरसेनः कथं तत्र यास्यते दारुकावने ।
कथमर्चिष्यति शिवं त्वं तद्वद महामते ॥
4.30.m: The sages said: / How will Vīrasena go there to the Dārukā forest? / How will he worship Śiva? Tell us that, O noble-minded one.

4.30.s:
sūta uvāca |
niṣadhe sundare deśe kṣatriyāṇāṃ kule ca saḥ |
mahāsenasuto vīrasenaścaiva śivapriyaḥ ||
4.30.d:
सूत उवाच ।
निषधे सुन्दरे देशे क्षत्रियाणां कुले च सः ।
महासेनसुतो वीरसेनश्चैव शिवप्रियः ॥
4.30.m: Sūta said: / In the beautiful land of Niṣadha, born in the lineage of the kṣatriyas, / was Vīrasena, the son of Mahāsena, beloved of Śiva.

4.30.s:
pārthiveśārcanaṃ kṛtvā tapaḥ paramaduṣkaram |
cakāra vīraseno vai varṣāṇāṃ dvādaśāvadhiḥ ||
4.30.d:
पार्थिवेशार्चनं कृत्वा तपः परमदुष्करम् ।
चकार वीरसेनो वै वर्षाणां द्वादशावधिः ॥
4.30.m: Having performed the worship of an earthen liṅga of Īśa, / Vīrasena performed exceedingly difficult austerity for a duration of twelve years.

4.30.s:
tataḥ prasanno deveśaḥ pratyakṣaṃ prāha śaṅkaraḥ |
kāṣṭhasya matsyikāṃ kṛtvā trapudhātuvilepanām ||
4.30.d:
ततः प्रसन्नो देवेशः प्रत्यक्षं प्राह शङ्करः ।
काष्ठस्य मत्स्यिकां कृत्वा त्रपुधातुविलेपनाम् ॥
4.30.m: Then Śaṅkara, the lord of the gods, pleased, spoke visibly: / 'Having made a small fish of wood smeared with the metal tin,

4.30.s:
vidhāya yogamāyāṃ ca dāsyāmi vīrasenaka |
tāṃ gṛhītvā praviśyainaṃ naubhiḥ saha vrajādhunā ||
4.30.d:
विधाय योगमायां च दास्यामि वीरसेनक ।
तां गृहीत्वा प्रविश्यैनं नौभिः सह व्रजाधुना ॥
4.30.m: and having infused it with yogamāyā, I will give it to you, O Vīrasenaka. / Taking it and entering here, proceed now along with boats.

4.30.s:
tatastvaṃ tatra gatvā ca vivare ca kṛte mayā |
praviśya ca tadā pūjāṃ kṛtvā nāgeśvarasya ca ||
4.30.d:
ततस्त्वं तत्र गत्वा च विवरे च कृते मया ।
प्रविश्य च तदा पूजां कृत्वा नागेश्वरस्य च ॥
4.30.m: Then, having gone there and entered the cavity made by me, / and having performed the worship of Nāgeśvara,

4.30.s:
tataḥ pāśupataṃ prāpya hatvā ca rākṣasīmukhān |
mayi dṛṣṭe tadā kiñcinnyūnaṃ te na bhaviṣyati ||
4.30.d:
ततः पाशुपतं प्राप्य हत्वा च राक्षसीमुखान् ।
मयि दृष्टे तदा किञ्चिन्न्यूनं ते न भविष्यति ॥
4.30.m: and then having obtained the Pāśupata weapon and slain the chief rākṣasīs, / once you have seen me, nothing will be lacking to you.

4.30.s:
pārvatyāśca balaṃ caiva sampūrṇaṃ vai bhaviṣyati |
anye ca mleccharūpā ye bhaviṣyanti vane śubhāḥ ||
4.30.d:
पार्वत्याश्च बलं चैव सम्पूर्णं वै भविष्यति ।
अन्ये च म्लेच्छरूपा ये भविष्यन्ति वने शुभाः ॥
4.30.m: The power of Pārvatī will also become complete; / and others who have the form of barbarians will become auspicious in the forest.'

4.30.s:
ityuktvā śaṅkarastatra vīrasenaṃ hi duḥkhahā |
kṛtvā kṛpāṃ ca mahatīṃ tatraivāntardadhe prabhuḥ ||
4.30.d:
इत्युक्त्वा शङ्करस्तत्र वीरसेनं हि दुःखहा ।
कृत्वा कृपां च महतीं तत्रैवान्तर्दधे प्रभुः ॥
4.30.m: Having spoken thus to Vīrasena there, Śaṅkara, the destroyer of sorrow, / bestowed great grace and vanished right there, the Lord.

4.30.s:
iti dattavaraḥ so'pi śivena paramātmanā |
śaktaḥ sarvaṃ tadā kartuṃ sambabhūva na saṃśayaḥ ||
4.30.d:
इति दत्तवरः सोऽपि शिवेन परमात्मना ।
शक्तः सर्वं तदा कर्तुं सम्बभूव न संशयः ॥
4.30.m: Granted the boon thus by Śiva, the Supreme Self, / he became capable of doing everything then, without a doubt.

4.30.s:
evaṃ nāgeśvaro deva utpanno jyotiṣāṃ patiḥ |
liṅgarūpastrilokasya sarvakāmapradaḥ sadā ||
4.30.d:
एवं नागेश्वरो देव उत्पन्नो ज्योतिषां पतिः ।
लिङ्गरूपस्त्रिलोकस्य सर्वकामप्रदः सदा ॥
4.30.m: Thus the god Nāgeśvara, the lord of the lights, / appeared in the form of a liṅga, granting all desires of the three worlds at all times.

4.30.s:
etadyaḥ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ nāgeśodbhavamādarāt |
sarvānkāmāniyāddhīmānmahāpātakanāśanān ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
caturthī koṭirudrasaṃhitā
4.30.d:
एतद्यः शृणुयान्नित्यं नागेशोद्भवमादरात् ।
सर्वान्कामानियाद्धीमान्महापातकनाशनान् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
चतुर्थी कोटिरुद्रसंहिता
4.30.m:
Whoever hears this origin of Nāgeśa daily with reverence, / that wise person shall attain all desires that destroy the great sins.

Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Eulogy of the Origin of the Nāgeśvara Liṅga of Light', in the fourth Koṭirudrasaṃhitā of the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

4.31.s:
sūta uvāca |
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi liṅgaṃ rāmeśvarābhidham |
utpannaṃ ca yathā pūrvamṛṣayaḥ śṛṇutādarāt ||
4.31.d:
सूत उवाच ।
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि लिङ्गं रामेश्वराभिधम् ।
उत्पन्नं च यथा पूर्वमृषयः शृणुतादरात् ॥
4.31.m: Sūta said: / Hereafter I shall declare the liṅga named Rāmeśvara, / and how it arose previously; listen with reverence, O sages.

4.31.s: purā viṣṇuḥ pṛthivyāṃ cāvatatāra satāṃ priyaḥ ||
4.31.d: पुरा विष्णुः पृथिव्यां चावततार सतां प्रियः ॥
4.31.m: Long ago, Viṣṇu, who is dear to the virtuous, descended to the earth.

4.31.s:
tatra sītā hṛtā viprā rāvaṇenorumāyinā |
prāpitā svagṛhaṃ sā hi laṅkāyāṃ janakātmajā ||
4.31.d:
तत्र सीता हृता विप्रा रावणेनोरुमायिना ।
प्रापिता स्वगृहं सा हि लङ्कायां जनकात्मजा ॥
4.31.m: There, O priests, Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, was abducted by Rāvaṇa of immense sorcery, / and was brought to his own home in Laṅkā.

4.31.s:
anveṣaṇaparastasyāḥ kiṣkindhākhyāṃ purīmagāt |
sugrīvahitakṛdbhūtvā vālinaṃ sañjaghāna ha ||
4.31.d:
अन्वेषणपरस्तस्याः किष्किन्धाख्यां पुरीमगात् ।
सुग्रीवहितकृद्भूत्वा वालिनं सञ्जघान ह ॥
4.31.m: Intent upon searching for her, he went to the city named Kiṣkindhā; / having become a benefactor of Sugrīva, he slew Vālin.

4.31.s:
tatra sthitvā kiyatkālaṃ tadanveṣaṇatatparaḥ |
sugrīvādyairlakṣmaṇena vicāraṃ kṛtavānsa vai ||
4.31.d:
तत्र स्थित्वा कियत्कालं तदन्वेषणतत्परः ।
सुग्रीवाद्यैर्लक्ष्मणेन विचारं कृतवान्स वै ॥
4.31.m: Remaining there for some time, intent upon searching for her, / he deliberated together with Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva and the others.

4.31.s:
kapīn sampreṣayāmāsa caturdikṣu nṛpātmajaḥ |
hanumatpramukhān rāmastadanveṣaṇahetave ||
4.31.d:
कपीन् सम्प्रेषयामास चतुर्दिक्षु नृपात्मजः ।
हनुमत्प्रमुखान् रामस्तदन्वेषणहेतवे ॥
4.31.m: The prince Rāma dispatched the monkeys / headed by Hanumat in the four directions for the purpose of searching for her.

4.31.s:
atha jñātvā gatāṃ laṅkāṃ sītāṃ kapivarānanāt |
sītācūḍāmaṇiṃ prāpya mumude so'ti rāghavaḥ ||
4.31.d:
अथ ज्ञात्वा गतां लङ्कां सीतां कपिवराननात् ।
सीताचूडामणिं प्राप्य मुमुदे सोऽति राघवः ॥
4.31.m: Then, learning from the mouth of the foremost of monkeys that Sītā had gone to Laṅkā, / and having received Sītā's crest-jewel, that descendant of Raghu rejoiced greatly.

4.31.s:
sakapīśastadā rāmo lakṣmaṇena yuto dvijāḥ |
sugrīvapramukhaiḥ puṇyairvānarairbalavattaraiḥ ||
4.31.d:
सकपीशस्तदा रामो लक्ष्मणेन युतो द्विजाः ।
सुग्रीवप्रमुखैः पुण्यैर्वानरैर्बलवत्तरैः ॥
4.31.m: Accompanied by the lord of monkeys, Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, O twice-born ones, / and with the exceedingly mighty, virtuous monkeys headed by Sugrīva,

4.31.s:
padmairaṣṭādaśākhyaiśca yayau tīraṃ payonidheḥ |
dakṣiṇe sāgare yo vai dṛśyate lavaṇākaraḥ ||
4.31.d:
पद्मैरष्टादशाख्यैश्च ययौ तीरं पयोनिधेः ।
दक्षिणे सागरे यो वै दृश्यते लवणाकरः ॥
4.31.m: numbering eighteen padmas, went to the shore of the ocean, / which is seen in the southern ocean as a repository of salt [water].

4.31.s:
tatrāgatya svayaṃ rāmo velāyāṃ saṃsthito hi saḥ |
vānaraiḥ sevyamānastu lakṣmaṇena śivapriyaḥ ||
4.31.d:
तत्रागत्य स्वयं रामो वेलायां संस्थितो हि सः ।
वानरैः सेव्यमानस्तु लक्ष्मणेन शिवप्रियः ॥
4.31.m: Having arrived there in person, Rāma stayed on the shore, / served by the monkeys and Lakṣmaṇa, he who is dear to Śiva.

4.31.s:
hā jānaki kuto yātā kadā ceyaṃ miliṣyati |
agādhaḥ sāgaraścaivātāryā senā ca vānarī ||
4.31.d:
हा जानकि कुतो याता कदा चेयं मिलिष्यति ।
अगाधः सागरश्चैवातार्या सेना च वानरी ॥
4.31.m: 'Alas, daughter of Janaka! Where have you gone? And when will she be met? / The ocean is unfathomable, and the army of monkeys must cross it.

4.31.s:
rākṣaso giridhartā ca mahābalaparākramaḥ |
laṅkākhyo durgamo durga indrajittanayo'sya vai ||
4.31.d:
राक्षसो गिरिधर्ता च महाबलपराक्रमः ।
लङ्काख्यो दुर्गमो दुर्ग इन्द्रजित्तनयोऽस्य वै ॥
4.31.m: The rākṣasa can lift mountains, possessed of great strength and valor; / the fortress named Laṅkā is impassable, and Indrajit is his son.'

4.31.s:
ityevaṃ sa vicāryaiva taṭe sthitvā salakṣmaṇaḥ |
āśvāsito vanaukobhiraṅgadādipuraḥ saraiḥ ||
4.31.d:
इत्येवं स विचार्यैव तटे स्थित्वा सलक्ष्मणः ।
आश्वासितो वनौकोभिरङ्गदादिपुरः सरैः ॥
4.31.m: Reflecting thus while standing on the shore with Lakṣmaṇa, / he was consoled by the forest-dwellers led by Aṅgada and others.

4.31.s:
etasminnantare tatra rāghavaḥ śaivasattamaḥ |
uvāca bhrātaraṃ prītyā jalārthī lakṣmaṇābhidham ||
4.31.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र राघवः शैवसत्तमः ।
उवाच भ्रातरं प्रीत्या जलार्थी लक्ष्मणाभिधम् ॥
4.31.m: In the meantime, the descendant of Raghu, the best of Śaivas, / desiring water, spoke affectionately to his brother named Lakṣmaṇa.

4.31.s:
śrīrāma uvāca |
bhrātarlakṣmaṇa vīreśāhaṃ jalārthī pipāsitaḥ |
tadānaya drutaṃ pātho vānaraiḥ kaiścideva hi ||
4.31.d:
श्रीराम उवाच ।
भ्रातर्लक्ष्मण वीरेशाहं जलार्थी पिपासितः ।
तदानय द्रुतं पाथो वानरैः कैश्चिदेव हि ॥
4.31.m: Glorious Rāma said: / 'Brother Lakṣmaṇa, lord of heroes, I desire water; I am thirsty. / Therefore, bring water quickly through some of the monkeys.'

4.31.s:
sūta uvāca |
tacchrutvā vānarāstatra hyadhāvanta diśo daśa |
nītvā jalaṃ ca te procuḥ praṇipatya puraḥ sthitāḥ ||
4.31.d:
सूत उवाच ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा वानरास्तत्र ह्यधावन्त दिशो दश ।
नीत्वा जलं च ते प्रोचुः प्रणिपत्य पुरः स्थिताः ॥
4.31.m: Sūta said: / Hearing that, the monkeys ran in the ten directions; / and having brought water, standing before him, they bowed down and said:

4.31.s:
vānarā ūcuḥ |
jalaṃ ca gṛhyatāṃ svāminnānītaṃ tattvadājñayā |
mahottamaṃ ca susvādu śītalaṃ prāṇatarpaṇam ||
4.31.d:
वानरा ऊचुः ।
जलं च गृह्यतां स्वामिन्नानीतं तत्त्वदाज्ञया ।
महोत्तमं च सुस्वादु शीतलं प्राणतर्पणम् ॥
4.31.m: The monkeys said: / 'Let the water be taken, O Master; it has been brought at your command. / It is exceedingly fine, very sweet, cool, and satisfying to the breath of life.'

4.31.s:
sūta uvāca |
suprasannataro bhūtvā kṛpādṛṣṭyā vilokya tān |
tacchrutvā rāmacandro'sau svayaṃ jagrāha tajjalam ||
4.31.d:
सूत उवाच ।
सुप्रसन्नतरो भूत्वा कृपादृष्ट्या विलोक्य तान् ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा रामचन्द्रोऽसौ स्वयं जग्राह तज्जलम् ॥
4.31.m: Sūta said: / Becoming exceedingly pleased and looking at them with a glance of grace, / hearing that, Rāmacandra took that water himself.

4.31.s:
sa śaivastajjalaṃ nītvā pātumārabdhavānyadā |
tadā ca smaraṇaṃ jātamitthamasya śivecchayā ||
4.31.d:
स शैवस्तज्जलं नीत्वा पातुमारब्धवान्यदा ।
तदा च स्मरणं जातमित्थमस्य शिवेच्छया ॥
4.31.m: When that Śaiva, having taken that water, was about to drink, / at that moment remembrance arose in him thus by the will of Śiva:

4.31.s:
na kṛtaṃ darśanaṃ śambhorgṛhyate ca jalaṃ katham |
svasvāminaḥ pareśasya sarvānandapradasya vai ||
4.31.d:
न कृतं दर्शनं शम्भोर्गृह्यते च जलं कथम् ।
स्वस्वामिनः परेशस्य सर्वानन्दप्रदस्य वै ॥
4.31.m: 'A vision of Śambhu has not been had; how can water be taken, / [the vision] of one's own Master, the Supreme Lord, the giver of all joy?'

4.31.s:
ityuktvā ca jalaṃ muktaṃ tadā raghuvareṇa ca |
paścācca pārthivīṃ pūjāṃ cakāra raghunandanaḥ ||
4.31.d:
इत्युक्त्वा च जलं मुक्तं तदा रघुवरेण च ।
पश्चाच्च पार्थिवीं पूजां चकार रघुनन्दनः ॥
4.31.m: Having spoken thus, the water was abandoned by the best of the Raghus; / and afterwards, the joy of the Raghus performed the worship of an earthen liṅga.

4.31.s:
āvāhanādikāṃścaiva hyupacārānprakalpya vai |
vidhivatṣoḍaśaṃ prītyā devamānarca śaṅkaram ||
4.31.d:
आवाहनादिकांश्चैव ह्युपचारान्प्रकल्प्य वै ।
विधिवत्षोडशं प्रीत्या देवमानर्च शङ्करम् ॥
4.31.m: Arranging the services such as the invocation, / he worshipped the god Śaṅkara according to rule with the sixteen [services] with love.

4.31.s:
praṇipātaiḥ stavairdivyaiḥ śivaṃ santoṣya yatnataḥ |
prārthayāmāsa sadbhaktyā sa rāmaḥ śaṅkaraṃ mudā ||
4.31.d:
प्रणिपातैः स्तवैर्दिव्यैः शिवं सन्तोष्य यत्नतः ।
प्रार्थयामास सद्भक्त्या स रामः शङ्करं मुदा ॥
4.31.m: Having carefully gratified Śiva with prostrations and divine hymns of praise, / that Rāma joyfully prayed to Śaṅkara with true devotion.

4.31.s:
śrīrāma uvāca |
svāmin śambho mahādeva sarvadā bhaktavatsala |
pāhi māṃ śaraṇāpannaṃ tvadbhaktaṃ dīnamānasam ||
4.31.d:
श्रीराम उवाच ।
स्वामिन् शम्भो महादेव सर्वदा भक्तवत्सल ।
पाहि मां शरणापन्नं त्वद्भक्तं दीनमानसम् ॥
4.31.m: Śrī Rāma said: / 'O Lord, O Śambhu, O Mahādeva, always affectionate toward devotees! / Protect me, who have taken refuge in you, your devotee whose mind is afflicted.

4.31.s:
etajjalamagādhaṃ ca vāridherbhavatāraṇa |
rāvaṇākhyo mahāvīro rākṣaso balavattaraḥ ||
4.31.d:
एतज्जलमगाधं च वारिधेर्भवतारण ।
रावणाख्यो महावीरो राक्षसो बलवत्तरः ॥
4.31.m: O savior from worldly existence, this water of the ocean is fathomless, / and the rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa is a mighty and exceedingly strong warrior.

4.31.s:
vānarāṇāṃ balaṃ hyetaccañcalaṃ yuddhasādhanam |
mama kāryaṃ kathaṃ siddhaṃ bhaviṣyati priyāptaye ||
4.31.d:
वानराणां बलं ह्येतच्चञ्चलं युद्धसाधनम् ।
मम कार्यं कथं सिद्धं भविष्यति प्रियाप्तये ॥
4.31.m: This army of monkeys, the means for battle, is fickle; / how will my purpose be accomplished for regaining my beloved?'

4.31.s:
tasmindeva tvayā kāryaṃ sāhāyyaṃ mama suvrata |
sāhāyyaṃ te vinā nātha mama kāryaṃ hi durlabham ||
4.31.d:
तस्मिन्देव त्वया कार्यं साहाय्यं मम सुव्रत ।
साहाय्यं ते विना नाथ मम कार्यं हि दुर्लभम् ॥
4.31.m: Therefore, O God, O you of noble vows, you must grant me assistance in this [undertaking]. / Indeed, without your assistance, O Lord, my objective is impossible to achieve.

4.31.s:
tvadīyo rāvaṇo'pīha durjayaḥ sarvathākhilaiḥ |
tvaddattavaradṛptaśca mahāvīrastrilokajit ||
4.31.d:
त्वदीयो रावणोऽपीह दुर्जयः सर्वथाखिलैः ।
त्वद्दत्तवरदृप्तश्च महावीरस्त्रिलोकजित् ॥
4.31.m: Moreover, your [devotee] Rāvaṇa is utterly invincible here by anyone; / proud on account of the boons granted by you, he is a great hero, conqueror of the three worlds.

4.31.s:
apyahaṃ tava dāso'smi tvadadhīnaśca sarvathā |
vicāryeti tvayā kāryaḥ pakṣapātaḥ sadāśiva ||
4.31.d:
अप्यहं तव दासोऽस्मि त्वदधीनश्च सर्वथा ।
विचार्येति त्वया कार्यः पक्षपातः सदाशिव ॥
4.31.m: Yet I too am your servant and entirely dependent upon you. / Considering this, you should show favoritism [to me], O Sadāśiva.

4.31.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityevaṃ sa ca samprārthya namaskṛtya punaḥ punaḥ |
tadā jaya jayetyuccairudghoṣaiḥ śaṅkareti ca ||
4.31.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्येवं स च सम्प्रार्थ्य नमस्कृत्य पुनः पुनः ।
तदा जय जयेत्युच्चैरुद्घोषैः शङ्करेति च ॥
4.31.m: Sūta said: / Having thus prayed and bowed down again and again, / he then [exclaimed] with loud shouts: "Victory! Victory!" and "O Śaṅkara!"

4.31.s:
iti stutvā śivaṃ tatra mantradhyānaparāyaṇaḥ |
punaḥ pūjāṃ tataḥ kṛtvā svāmyagre sa nanarta ha ||
4.31.d:
इति स्तुत्वा शिवं तत्र मन्त्रध्यानपरायणः ।
पुनः पूजां ततः कृत्वा स्वाम्यग्रे स ननर्त ह ॥
4.31.m: Having thus praised Śiva there, devoted to mantras and meditation, / he then performed worship once more and danced before the Lord.

4.31.s:
premaviklinnahṛdayo gallanādaṃ yadākarot |
tadā ca śaṅkaro devaḥ suprasanno babhūva ha ||
4.31.d:
प्रेमविक्लिन्नहृदयो गल्लनादं यदाकरोत् ।
तदा च शङ्करो देवः सुप्रसन्नो बभूव ह ॥
4.31.m: When his heart melted with love and he made resonant throat-sounds, / Lord Śaṅkara then became exceedingly pleased.

4.31.s:
sāṅgaḥ saparivāraśca jyotīrūpo maheśvaraḥ |
yathoktarūpamamalaṃ kṛtvāvirabhavad drutam ||
4.31.d:
साङ्गः सपरिवारश्च ज्योतीरूपो महेश्वरः ।
यथोक्तरूपममलं कृत्वाविरभवद् द्रुतम् ॥
4.31.m: Accompanied by his limbs and attendants, having the nature of light, Maheśvara, / assuming his spotless form as described [in scripture], manifested swiftly.

4.31.s:
tataḥ santuṣṭahṛdayo rāmabhaktyā maheśvaraḥ |
śivamastu varaṃ brūhi rāmeti sa tadābravīt ||
4.31.d:
ततः सन्तुष्टहृदयो रामभक्त्या महेश्वरः ।
शिवमस्तु वरं ब्रूहि रामेति स तदाब्रवीत् ॥
4.31.m: Then Maheśvara, his heart pleased by Rāma's devotion, / said to him at that time: "May it be auspicious! Ask a boon, O Rāma!"

4.31.s:
tadrūpaṃ ca tadā dṛṣṭavā sarve pūtāstataḥ svayam |
kṛtavān rāghavaḥ pūjāṃ śivadharmaparāyaṇaḥ ||
4.31.d:
तद्रूपं च तदा दृष्टवा सर्वे पूतास्ततः स्वयम् ।
कृतवान् राघवः पूजां शिवधर्मपरायणः ॥
4.31.m: Beholding that form then, all of them were purified on the spot. / Rāghava, devoted to the duties of Śiva, performed worship.

4.31.s:
stutiṃ ca vividhāṃ kṛtvā praṇipatya śivaṃ mudā |
jayaṃ ca prārthayāmāsa rāvaṇājau tadātmanaḥ ||
4.31.d:
स्तुतिं च विविधां कृत्वा प्रणिपत्य शिवं मुदा ।
जयं च प्रार्थयामास रावणाजौ तदात्मनः ॥
4.31.m: Having offered various praises and bowed down joyfully to Śiva, / he then prayed for his own victory in the battle with Rāvaṇa.

4.31.s:
tataḥ prasannahṛdayo rāmabhaktyā maheśvaraḥ |
jayo'stu te mahārāja prītyā sa punarabravīt ||
4.31.d:
ततः प्रसन्नहृदयो रामभक्त्या महेश्वरः ।
जयोऽस्तु ते महाराज प्रीत्या स पुनरब्रवीत् ॥
4.31.m: Then Maheśvara, his heart delighted by Rāma's devotion, / spoke again with affection: "May victory be yours, O Great King!"

4.31.s:
śivadattaṃ jayaṃ prāpya hyanujñāṃ samavāpya ca |
punaśca prārthayāmāsa sāñjalirnatamastakaḥ ||
4.31.d:
शिवदत्तं जयं प्राप्य ह्यनुज्ञां समवाप्य च ।
पुनश्च प्रार्थयामास साञ्जलिर्नतमस्तकः ॥
4.31.m: Having obtained victory granted by Śiva and having received his permission, / he prayed once more with folded hands and bent head.

4.31.s:
śrīrāma uvāca |
tvayā stheyamiha svāmiṃllokānāṃ pāvanāya ca |
pareṣāmupakārārthaṃ yadi tuṣṭo'si śaṅkara ||
4.31.d:
श्रीराम उवाच ।
त्वया स्थेयमिह स्वामिंल्लोकानां पावनाय च ।
परेषामुपकारार्थं यदि तुष्टोऽसि शङ्कर ॥
4.31.m: Śrī Rāma said: / You must abide here, O Lord, to purify the worlds / and for the welfare of others, if you are pleased, O Śaṅkara.

4.31.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityuktastu śivastatra liṅgarūpo'bhavattadā |
rāmeśvaraśca nāmnā vai prasiddho jagatītale ||
4.31.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्युक्तस्तु शिवस्तत्र लिङ्गरूपोऽभवत्तदा ।
रामेश्वरश्च नाम्ना वै प्रसिद्धो जगतीतले ॥
4.31.m: Sūta said: / Thus addressed, Śiva then took the form of a liṅga there; / he indeed became famous on the earth by the name Rāmeśvara.

4.31.s:
rāmastu tatprabhāvādvai sindhumuttīrya cāñjasā |
rāvaṇādīnnihatyāśu rākṣasānprāpa tāṃ priyām ||
4.31.d:
रामस्तु तत्प्रभावाद्वै सिन्धुमुत्तीर्य चाञ्जसा ।
रावणादीन्निहत्याशु राक्षसान्प्राप तां प्रियाम् ॥
4.31.m: And Rāma, by that power indeed, crossed the ocean easily, / quickly slew Rāvaṇa and the other demons, and recovered his beloved.

4.31.s:
rāmeśvarasya mahimādbhuto'bhūdbhuvi cātulaḥ |
bhuktimuktipradaścaiva sarvadā bhaktakāmadaḥ ||
4.31.d:
रामेश्वरस्य महिमाद्भुतोऽभूद्भुवि चातुलः ।
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदश्चैव सर्वदा भक्तकामदः ॥
4.31.m: Incomparable and marvelous on earth was the greatness of Rāmeśvara, / bestowing enjoyment and liberation, ever fulfilling the desires of devotees.

4.31.s:
divyagaṅgājalenaiva snāpayiṣyati yaḥ śivam |
rāmeśvaraṃ ca sadbhaktyā sa jīvanmukta eva hi ||
4.31.d:
दिव्यगङ्गाजलेनैव स्नापयिष्यति यः शिवम् ।
रामेश्वरं च सद्भक्त्या स जीवन्मुक्त एव हि ॥
4.31.m: Whoever bathes Śiva, Rāmeśvara, with the divine water of the Gaṅgā / with true devotion, is indeed liberated while living.

4.31.s:
iha bhuktvākhilānbhogāndevānāṃ durlabhānapi |
ante prāpya paraṃ jñānaṃ kaivalyaṃ prāpnuyād dhruvam ||
4.31.d:
इह भुक्त्वाखिलान्भोगान्देवानां दुर्लभानपि ।
अन्ते प्राप्य परं ज्ञानं कैवल्यं प्राप्नुयाद् ध्रुवम् ॥
4.31.m: Having enjoyed all pleasures here, even those difficult for the gods to attain, / and obtaining supreme knowledge at the end, he surely attains absolute liberation.

4.31.s:
iti vaśca samākhyātaṃ jyotirligaṃ śivasya tu |
rāmeśvarābhidhaṃ divyaṃ śṛṇvatāṃ pāpahārakam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
caturthī koṭirudrasaṃhitā
4.31.d:
इति वश्च समाख्यातं ज्योतिर्लिगं शिवस्य तु ।
रामेश्वराभिधं दिव्यं शृण्वतां पापहारकम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
चतुर्थी कोटिरुद्रसंहिता
4.31.m:
Thus has been described to you the divine jyotirliṅga of Śiva, / named Rāmeśvara, which removes sins for those who hear of it.

Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Rāmeśvara,' in the Koṭirudrasaṃhitā, the fourth [book] of the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

4.32.s:
sūta uvāca |
ataḥ paraṃ ca ghuśmeśaṃ jyotirliṅgamudāhṛtam |
tasyaiva ca sumāhātmyaṃ śrūyatāmṛṣisattamāḥ ||
4.32.d:
सूत उवाच ।
अतः परं च घुश्मेशं ज्योतिर्लिङ्गमुदाहृतम् ।
तस्यैव च सुमाहात्म्यं श्रूयतामृषिसत्तमाः ॥
4.32.m: Sūta said: / Hereafter is recounted the jyotirliṅga Ghuśmeśa; / hear its excellent eulogy, O best of sages.

4.32.s:
dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi śreṣṭho girirdeveti saṃjñakaḥ |
mahāśobhānvito nityaṃ rājate'dbhutadarśanaḥ ||
4.32.d:
दक्षिणस्यां दिशि श्रेष्ठो गिरिर्देवेति संज्ञकः ।
महाशोभान्वितो नित्यं राजतेऽद्भुतदर्शनः ॥
4.32.m: In the southern direction, an excellent mountain named Devagiri / constantly shines, endowed with great splendor and wondrous to behold.

4.32.s:
tasyaiva nikaṭe kaścidbhāradvājakulodbhavaḥ |
sudharmā nāma vipraśca nyavasad brahmavittamaḥ ||
4.32.d:
तस्यैव निकटे कश्चिद्भारद्वाजकुलोद्भवः ।
सुधर्मा नाम विप्रश्च न्यवसद् ब्रह्मवित्तमः ॥
4.32.m: Near that very mountain lived a brahmin born in the lineage of Bharadvāja, / named Sudharmā, the best of knowers of the absolute.

4.32.s:
tasya priyā sudehā ca śivadharmaparāyaṇā |
patisevāparā nityaṃ gṛhakarmavicakṣaṇā ||
4.32.d:
तस्य प्रिया सुदेहा च शिवधर्मपरायणा ।
पतिसेवापरा नित्यं गृहकर्मविचक्षणा ॥
4.32.m: His beloved wife was Sudehā, devoted to the duties of Śiva, / ever intent on serving her husband, and skilled in household duties.

4.32.s:
sudharmā ca dvijaśreṣṭho devatātithipūjakaḥ |
vedamārgaparo nityamagnisevāparāyaṇaḥ ||
4.32.d:
सुधर्मा च द्विजश्रेष्ठो देवतातिथिपूजकः ।
वेदमार्गपरो नित्यमग्निसेवापरायणः ॥
4.32.m: And Sudharmā, the best of the twice-born, was a worshiper of deities and guests, / ever intent upon the Vedic path, and devoted to serving the sacred fire.

4.32.s:
trikālasandhyayā yuktaḥ sūryarūpasamadyutiḥ |
śiṣyāṇāṃ pāṭhakaścaiva vedaśāstravicakṣaṇaḥ ||
4.32.d:
त्रिकालसन्ध्यया युक्तः सूर्यरूपसमद्युतिः ।
शिष्याणां पाठकश्चैव वेदशास्त्रविचक्षणः ॥
4.32.m: Endowed with [worship at] the three daily twilights, his radiance equal to the sun's form, / he was a teacher of disciples, learned in the Vedas and treatises.

4.32.s:
dhanavāṃśca paro dātā saujanyaguṇabhājanaḥ |
śivakarmarato nityaṃ śaivaḥ śaivajanapriyaḥ ||
4.32.d:
धनवांश्च परो दाता सौजन्यगुणभाजनः ।
शिवकर्मरतो नित्यं शैवः शैवजनप्रियः ॥
4.32.m: He was wealthy, an eminent giver, a vessel of virtues and kindness, / ever engaged in rites for Śiva, a Śaiva dear to Śaiva people.

4.32.s:
āyurbahu vyatīyāya tasya dharmaṃ prakurvataḥ |
putraśca nābhavattasya ṛtuḥ syādaphalaḥ striyāḥ ||
4.32.d:
आयुर्बहु व्यतीयाय तस्य धर्मं प्रकुर्वतः ।
पुत्रश्च नाभवत्तस्य ऋतुः स्यादफलः स्त्रियाः ॥
4.32.m: Much of his lifespan passed as he practiced righteousness; / yet he had no son, for the woman's fertile period was fruitless.

4.32.s:
tena duḥkhaṃ kṛtaṃ naiva vastujñānapareṇa hi |
ātmanastārakaścātmā hyātmanaḥ pāvanaśca saḥ ||
4.32.d:
तेन दुःखं कृतं नैव वस्तुज्ञानपरेण हि ।
आत्मनस्तारकश्चात्मा ह्यात्मनः पावनश्च सः ॥
4.32.m: Devoted to the knowledge of reality, he did not grieve at all; / for the self is its own savior, and it is its own purifier.

4.32.s:
ityevaṃ mānasaṃ dhṛtvā duḥkhaṃ na kṛtavānstadā |
sudehā ca tadā duḥkhaṃ cakārāputrasambhavam ||
4.32.d:
इत्येवं मानसं धृत्वा दुःखं न कृतवान्स्तदा ।
सुदेहा च तदा दुःखं चकारापुत्रसम्भवम् ॥
4.32.m: Having established this in his mind, he did not grieve at that time; / but Sudehā then grieved over being sonless.

4.32.s:
nityaṃ ca svāminaṃ sā vai prārthayadyatnasādhane |
putrotpādanahetośca sarvavidyāviśāradam ||
4.32.d:
नित्यं च स्वामिनं सा वै प्रार्थयद्यत्नसाधने ।
पुत्रोत्पादनहेतोश्च सर्वविद्याविशारदम् ॥
4.32.m: She constantly begged her husband, who was expert in all sciences, / to undertake an effort for the sake of begetting a son.

4.32.s:
so'pi striyaṃ tadābhartsya kiṃ putraśca kariṣyati |
kā mātā kaḥ pitā putraḥ ko bandhuśca priyaśca kaḥ ||
4.32.d:
सोऽपि स्त्रियं तदाभर्त्स्य किं पुत्रश्च करिष्यति ।
का माता कः पिता पुत्रः को बन्धुश्च प्रियश्च कः ॥
4.32.m: He too then scolded the woman: "What will a son do? / Who is a mother, who is a father, who is a son, who is a relative, and who is dear?

4.32.s:
sarvaṃ svārthaparaṃ devi trilokyāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ |
jānīhi tvaṃ viśeṣeṇa buddhyā śokaṃ na vai kuru ||
4.32.d:
सर्वं स्वार्थपरं देवि त्रिलोक्यां नात्र संशयः ।
जानीहि त्वं विशेषेण बुद्ध्या शोकं न वै कुरु ॥
4.32.m: Everything in the three worlds is selfishly motivated, O lady, there is no doubt about this; / understand this clearly through your intellect, and do not grieve!

4.32.s:
tasmāddevi tvayā duḥkhaṃ tyajanīyaṃ suniścitam |
nityaṃ mahyaṃ tvayā naiva kathanīyaṃ śubhavrate ||
4.32.d:
तस्माद्देवि त्वया दुःखं त्यजनीयं सुनिश्चितम् ।
नित्यं मह्यं त्वया नैव कथनीयं शुभव्रते ॥
4.32.m: Therefore, O lady, sorrow must certainly be abandoned by you; / you should not speak to me [about this] every day, O woman of auspicious vows!"

4.32.s:
evaṃ tāṃ sannivāryaiva bhagavaddharmatatparaḥ |
āsītparamasantuṣṭo dvandvaduḥkhaṃ samatyajat ||
4.32.d:
एवं तां सन्निवार्यैव भगवद्धर्मतत्परः ।
आसीत्परमसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वदुःखं समत्यजत् ॥
4.32.m: Having thus restrained her, intent on the divine law, / he remained supremely contented and cast aside the suffering of opposites.

4.32.s:
kadācicca sudehā vai gehe ca sahavāsinaḥ |
jagāma priyagoṣṭhyarthaṃ vivādastatra saṅgataḥ ||
4.32.d:
कदाचिच्च सुदेहा वै गेहे च सहवासिनः ।
जगाम प्रियगोष्ठ्यर्थं विवादस्तत्र सङ्गतः ॥
4.32.m: Once, Sudehā went to the house of a neighbor / for a friendly conversation, and a quarrel arose there.

4.32.s:
tatpatnī strīsvabhāvācca bhartsitā sā tayā tadā |
uktā ceti duruktyā vai sudehā viprakāminī ||
4.32.d:
तत्पत्नी स्त्रीस्वभावाच्च भर्त्सिता सा तया तदा ।
उक्ता चेति दुरुक्त्या वै सुदेहा विप्रकामिनी ॥
4.32.m: And by the [neighbor's] wife, out of a woman's nature, she was scolded then; / and with harsh words, Sudehā, the brahmin's beloved, was addressed thus:

4.32.s:
patnyuvāca |
aputriṇi kathaṃ garvaṃ kuruṣe putriṇī hyaham |
maddhanaṃ bhokṣyate putro dhanaṃ te kaśca bhokṣyate ||
4.32.d:
पत्न्युवाच ।
अपुत्रिणि कथं गर्वं कुरुषे पुत्रिणी ह्यहम् ।
मद्धनं भोक्ष्यते पुत्रो धनं ते कश्च भोक्ष्यते ॥
4.32.m: The wife said: / "Childless woman, why do you take pride, since I have children? / My son will enjoy my wealth; who will enjoy your wealth?

4.32.s:
nūnaṃ hariṣyate rājā tvaddhanaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ |
dhigdhiktvāṃ te dhanaṃ dhikca dhik te mānaṃ hi vandhyake ||
4.32.d:
नूनं हरिष्यते राजा त्वद्धनं नात्र संशयः ।
धिग्धिक्त्वां ते धनं धिक्च धिक् ते मानं हि वन्ध्यके ॥
4.32.m: Surely the king will seize your wealth, of this there is no doubt; / fie, fie on you, and fie on your wealth, and fie on your pride, O barren woman!"

4.32.s:
sūta uvāca |
bhartsitā tābhiriti sā gṛhamāgatya duḥkhitā |
svāmine kathayāmāsa taduktaṃ sarvamādarāt ||
4.32.d:
सूत उवाच ।
भर्त्सिता ताभिरिति सा गृहमागत्य दुःखिता ।
स्वामिने कथयामास तदुक्तं सर्वमादरात् ॥
4.32.m: Sūta said: / Thus scolded by them, she came home distressed, / and related respectfully to her husband all that had been said.

4.32.s:
brāhmaṇo'pi tadā duḥkhaṃ na cakāra subuddhimān |
kathitaṃ kathyatāmeva yadbhāvi tadbhavetpriye ||
4.32.d:
ब्राह्मणोऽपि तदा दुःखं न चकार सुबुद्धिमान् ।
कथितं कथ्यतामेव यद्भावि तद्भवेत्प्रिये ॥
4.32.m: Even then, the wise brahmin did not grieve: / "What has been said, let it be said; whatever is to happen will happen, my dear."

4.32.s:
ityevaṃ ca tadā tena hyāśvastāpi punaḥ punaḥ |
na tadā sātyajadduḥkhaṃ hyāgrahaṃ kṛtavatyasau ||
sudehovāca ||
4.32.d:
इत्येवं च तदा तेन ह्याश्वस्तापि पुनः पुनः ।
न तदा सात्यजद्दुःखं ह्याग्रहं कृतवत्यसौ ॥
सुदेहोवाच ॥
4.32.m: Although consoled again and again by him in this manner, / she did not abandon her grief then, and remained obstinate.

4.32.s:
yathā tathā tvayā putraḥ samutpādyaḥ priyo'si me |
tyakṣayāmi hyanyathāhaṃ ca dehaṃ dehabhṛtāṃ vara ||
4.32.d:
यथा तथा त्वया पुत्रः समुत्पाद्यः प्रियोऽसि मे ।
त्यक्षयामि ह्यन्यथाहं च देहं देहभृतां वर ॥
4.32.m: "By any means you must beget a son; you are dear to me. / Otherwise, I shall abandon my body, O best of embodied beings!"

4.32.s:
sūta uvāca |
evamuktaṃ tayā śrutvā sudharmā brāhmaṇottamaḥ |
śivaṃ sasmāra manasā tadāgrahanipīḍitaḥ ||
4.32.d:
सूत उवाच ।
एवमुक्तं तया श्रुत्वा सुधर्मा ब्राह्मणोत्तमः ।
शिवं सस्मार मनसा तदाग्रहनिपीडितः ॥
4.32.m: Sūta said: / Hearing what she said, Sudharmā, the best of brahmins, / afflicted by her insistence, remembered Śiva in his mind.

4.32.s:
agneragre'kṣipatpuṣpadvayaṃ vipro hyatandritaḥ |
manasā dakṣiṇaṃ puṣpaṃ tanmene putrakāmadam ||
4.32.d:
अग्नेरग्रेऽक्षिपत्पुष्पद्वयं विप्रो ह्यतन्द्रितः ।
मनसा दक्षिणं पुष्पं तन्मेने पुत्रकामदम् ॥
4.32.m: The unwearied brahmin cast two flowers before the fire; / in his mind, he considered the right flower as granting the desire for a son.

4.32.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā paṇaṃ patnīmuvāca brāhmaṇaḥ sa ca |
anayorgrāhyamekaṃ te puṣpaṃ putraphalāptaye ||
4.32.d:
एवं कृत्वा पणं पत्नीमुवाच ब्राह्मणः स च ।
अनयोर्ग्राह्यमेकं ते पुष्पं पुत्रफलाप्तये ॥
4.32.m: Having made such a wager, that brahmin said to his wife: / 'One flower of these two must be taken by you to obtain the fruit of a son.'

4.32.s:
tayā ca manasā dhṛtvā putraścaiva bhavenmama |
tadā ca svāminā yacca dhṛtaṃ puṣpaṃ sametu mām ||
4.32.d:
तया च मनसा धृत्वा पुत्रश्चैव भवेन्मम ।
तदा च स्वामिना यच्च धृतं पुष्पं समेतु माम् ॥
4.32.m: And keeping in mind: 'May I indeed have a son; / then may the flower which was held by my husband come to me!'

4.32.s:
ityuktvā ca tayā tatra namaskṛtya śivaṃ tadā |
natvā cāgniṃ punaḥ prārthya gṛhītaṃ puṣpamekakam ||
4.32.d:
इत्युक्त्वा च तया तत्र नमस्कृत्य शिवं तदा ।
नत्वा चाग्निं पुनः प्रार्थ्य गृहीतं पुष्पमेककम् ॥
4.32.m: Having said this, she bowed down to Śiva there, / bowed to the fire, prayed again, and took one flower.

4.32.s:
svāminā cintitaṃ yacca tad gṛhītaṃ tayā na hi |
sudehayā vimohena śivecchāsambhavena vai ||
4.32.d:
स्वामिना चिन्तितं यच्च तद् गृहीतं तया न हि ।
सुदेहया विमोहेन शिवेच्छासम्भवेन वै ॥
4.32.m: The one thought of by her husband was not taken by her, / due to the delusion of Sudehā, brought about indeed by the will of Śiva.

4.32.s:
tad dṛṣṭvā puruṣaścaiva niḥśvāsaṃ paryamocayat |
smṛtvā śivapadāmbhojamuvāca nijakāminīm ||
4.32.d:
तद् दृष्ट्वा पुरुषश्चैव निःश्वासं पर्यमोचयत् ।
स्मृत्वा शिवपदाम्भोजमुवाच निजकामिनीम् ॥
4.32.m: Seeing that, the man breathed a deep sigh; / remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, he spoke to his beloved wife.

4.32.s:
sudharmovāca |
nirmitaṃ ceśvareṇaiva kathaṃ caivānyathā bhavet |
āśāṃ tyaja priye tvaṃ ca paricaryāṃ kuru prabhoḥ ||
4.32.d:
सुधर्मोवाच ।
निर्मितं चेश्वरेणैव कथं चैवान्यथा भवेत् ।
आशां त्यज प्रिये त्वं च परिचर्यां कुरु प्रभोः ॥
4.32.m: Sudharmā said: / 'What is ordained by Īśvara alone—how could it turn out otherwise? / Abandon hope, my dear, and render service to the Lord.'

4.32.s:
ityuktvā tu svayaṃ vipra āśāṃ parivihāya ca |
dharmakāryarataḥ so'bhūcchaṅkaradhyānatatparaḥ ||
4.32.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तु स्वयं विप्र आशां परिविहाय च ।
धर्मकार्यरतः सोऽभूच्छङ्करध्यानतत्परः ॥
4.32.m: Having said this, the brahmin himself abandoned hope / and became devoted to righteous deeds, intent on meditating upon Śaṅkara.

4.32.s:
sā sudehāgrahaṃ naiva mumocātmajakāmyayā |
pratyuvāca patiṃ premṇā sāñjalirnatamastakā ||
4.32.d:
सा सुदेहाग्रहं नैव मुमोचात्मजकाम्यया ।
प्रत्युवाच पतिं प्रेम्णा साञ्जलिर्नतमस्तका ॥
4.32.m: Sudehā did not at all abandon her insistence, through the desire for a son; / with folded hands and bowed head, she replied to her husband with love.

4.32.s:
sudehovāca |
mayi putro na cāstvanyāṃ patnīṃ kuru madājñayā |
tasyāṃ nūnaṃ sutaścaiva bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
4.32.d:
सुदेहोवाच ।
मयि पुत्रो न चास्त्वन्यां पत्नीं कुरु मदाज्ञया ।
तस्यां नूनं सुतश्चैव भविष्यति न संशयः ॥
4.32.m: Sudehā said: / 'Let there be no son in me; take another wife by my command. / In her, a son will surely be born; there is no doubt.'

4.32.s:
sūta uvāca |
tadaiva prarthito vai sa brahmaṇaḥ śaivasattamaḥ |
uvāca svapriyāṃ tāṃ ca sudehāṃ dharmatatparaḥ ||
4.32.d:
सूत उवाच ।
तदैव प्रर्थितो वै स ब्रह्मणः शैवसत्तमः ।
उवाच स्वप्रियां तां च सुदेहां धर्मतत्परः ॥
4.32.m: Sūta said: / Thus entreatied at that time, that brahmin, the best of Śaivas, / devoted to righteousness, spoke to his beloved Sudehā.

4.32.s:
sudharmovāca |
tvadīyaṃ ca madīyaṃ ca sarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ gataṃ dhruvam |
tasmāttvaṃ dharmavighnaṃ ca priye mā kuru sāmpratam ||
4.32.d:
सुधर्मोवाच ।
त्वदीयं च मदीयं च सर्वं दुःखं गतं ध्रुवम् ।
तस्मात्त्वं धर्मविघ्नं च प्रिये मा कुरु साम्प्रतम् ॥
4.32.m: Sudharmā said: / 'Yours and mine—all sorrow is certainly gone. / Therefore, my dear, do not cause an obstacle to righteousness now.'

4.32.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityevaṃ vāritā sā ca svamātuḥ putrikāṃ tadā |
gṛhamānīya bhartāraṃ vṛṇu tvenāmidaṃ jagau ||
4.32.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्येवं वारिता सा च स्वमातुः पुत्रिकां तदा ।
गृहमानीय भर्तारं वृणु त्वेनामिदं जगौ ॥
4.32.m: Sūta said: / Thus prevented, she brought her mother's daughter to the house at that time / and said to her husband: 'Marry her!'

4.32.s:
sudharmovāca |
idānīṃ vadasi tvaṃ ca matpriyeyaṃ tataḥ punaḥ |
putrasūśca yadā syādvai tadā spardhāṃ kariṣyasi ||
4.32.d:
सुधर्मोवाच ।
इदानीं वदसि त्वं च मत्प्रियेयं ततः पुनः ।
पुत्रसूश्च यदा स्याद्वै तदा स्पर्धां करिष्यसि ॥
4.32.m: Sudharmā said: / 'Now you say: "She is dear to me"; but thereafter, / when she becomes the bearer of a son, you will become envious.'

4.32.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityuktā tena patinā sā sudehā ca tatpriyā |
punaḥ prāha karau baddhvā sudharmāṇaṃ patiṃ dvijāḥ ||
4.32.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्युक्ता तेन पतिना सा सुदेहा च तत्प्रिया ।
पुनः प्राह करौ बद्ध्वा सुधर्माणं पतिं द्विजाः ॥
4.32.m: Sūta said: / Addressed thus by her husband, that Sudehā, his beloved, / joining her hands, spoke again to her husband Sudharmā, O twice-born ones:

4.32.s:
nāhaṃ spardhāṃ bhaginyā vai kariṣye dvijasattama |
upayacchasva putrārthamimāmājñāpayāmi ca ||
4.32.d:
नाहं स्पर्धां भगिन्या वै करिष्ये द्विजसत्तम ।
उपयच्छस्व पुत्रार्थमिमामाज्ञापयामि च ॥
4.32.m: 'I will not bear envy toward my sister, O best of the twice-born. / Marry her for the sake of a son; I urge you.'

4.32.s:
ityevaṃ prārthitaḥ so'pi sudharmā priyayā tayā |
ghuśmāṃ tāṃ samupāyaṃsta vivāhavidhinā dvijaḥ ||
4.32.d:
इत्येवं प्रार्थितः सोऽपि सुधर्मा प्रियया तया ।
घुश्मां तां समुपायंस्त विवाहविधिना द्विजः ॥
4.32.m: Thus requested by his beloved, that twice-born Sudharmā / married Ghuśmā according to the wedding rites.

4.32.s:
tatastāṃ pariṇīyātha prārthayāmāsa tāṃ dvijaḥ |
tvadīyeyaṃ kaniṣṭhā hi sadā poṣyā'naghe priye ||
4.32.d:
ततस्तां परिणीयाथ प्रार्थयामास तां द्विजः ।
त्वदीयेयं कनिष्ठा हि सदा पोष्याऽनघे प्रिये ॥
4.32.m: Then, having wedded her, the twice-born requested her [Sudehā]: / 'This is your younger sister, O sinless, beloved one; she must always be cherished.'

4.32.s:
uktvaivaṃ sa ca dharmātmā sudharmā śaivasattamaḥ |
yathāyogyaṃ cakārāśu dharmasaṅgrahamātmanaḥ ||
4.32.d:
उक्त्वैवं स च धर्मात्मा सुधर्मा शैवसत्तमः ।
यथायोग्यं चकाराशु धर्मसङ्ग्रहमात्मनः ॥
4.32.m: Having spoken thus, the righteous Sudharmā, the best of Śaivas, / quickly accumulated his merit as was appropriate.

4.32.s:
sā cāpi mātṛputrīṃ tāṃ sakhīvatparyavarttata |
parityajya virodhaṃ hi pupoṣāharniśaṃ priyā ||
4.32.d:
सा चापि मातृपुत्रीं तां सखीवत्पर्यवर्त्तत ।
परित्यज्य विरोधं हि पुपोषाहर्निशं प्रिया ॥
4.32.m: And she too behaved toward her mother's daughter like a friend; / abandoning enmity, the beloved cherished [her] day and night.

4.32.s:
kaniṣṭhā caiva yā patnī svasranujñāmavāpya ca |
pārthivānsā cakārāśu nityamekottaraṃ śatam ||
4.32.d:
कनिष्ठा चैव या पत्नी स्वस्रनुज्ञामवाप्य च ।
पार्थिवान्सा चकाराशु नित्यमेकोत्तरं शतम् ॥
4.32.m: Having obtained the permission of her elder sister, the younger wife / quickly made one hundred and one earthen [liṅgas] every day.

4.32.s:
vidhānapūrvakaṃ ghuśmā sopacārasamanvitam |
kṛtvā tānprākṣipattatra taḍāge nikaṭasthite ||
4.32.d:
विधानपूर्वकं घुश्मा सोपचारसमन्वितम् ।
कृत्वा तान्प्राक्षिपत्तत्र तडागे निकटस्थिते ॥
4.32.m: Having duly fashioned them along with the rituals, / Ghuśmā threw them into the pond situated nearby.

4.32.s:
evaṃ nityaṃ sā cakāra śivapūjāṃ svakāmadām |
visṛjya punarāvāhya tatsaparyyāvidhānataḥ ||
4.32.d:
एवं नित्यं सा चकार शिवपूजां स्वकामदाम् ।
विसृज्य पुनरावाह्य तत्सपर्य्याविधानतः ॥
4.32.m: Thus every day she performed the worship of Śiva that grants one's desires, / dismissing and invoking anew according to the rite of his worship.

4.32.s:
kurvantyā nityamevaṃ hi tasyāḥ śaṅkarapūjanam |
lakṣasaṅkhyābhavatpūrṇā sarvakāmaphalapradā ||
4.32.d:
कुर्वन्त्या नित्यमेवं हि तस्याः शङ्करपूजनम् ।
लक्षसङ्ख्याभवत्पूर्णा सर्वकामफलप्रदा ॥
4.32.m: As she performed the worship of Śaṅkara daily in this manner, / the number of one hundred thousand was completed, granting the fruit of all desires.

4.32.s:
kṛpayā śaṅkarasyaiva tasyāḥ putro vyajāyata |
sundaraḥ subhagaścaiva kalyāṇaguṇabhājanaḥ ||
4.32.d:
कृपया शङ्करस्यैव तस्याः पुत्रो व्यजायत ।
सुन्दरः सुभगश्चैव कल्याणगुणभाजनः ॥
4.32.m: By the grace of Śaṅkara himself, a son was born to her— / handsome, fortunate, and a vessel of auspicious virtues.

4.32.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītaḥ sa vipro dharmavittamaḥ |
anāsaktaḥ sukhaṃ bheje jñānadharmaparāyaṇaḥ ||
4.32.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतः स विप्रो धर्मवित्तमः ।
अनासक्तः सुखं भेजे ज्ञानधर्मपरायणः ॥
4.32.m: Seeing him, the brahmin, foremost among knowers of righteousness, was exceedingly pleased; / unattached, devoted to knowledge and righteousness, he experienced joy.

4.32.s:
sudehā tāvadasyāstu spardhāmugrāṃ cakāra sā |
prathamaṃ śītalaṃ tasyā hṛdayaṃ hyasivatpunaḥ ||
4.32.d:
सुदेहा तावदस्यास्तु स्पर्धामुग्रां चकार सा ।
प्रथमं शीतलं तस्या हृदयं ह्यसिवत्पुनः ॥
4.32.m: Sudehā, meanwhile, felt fierce envy toward her; / at first her heart was cool, but again it became like a sword.

4.32.s:
tataḥ paraṃ ca yajjātaṃ kutsitaṃ karma duḥkhadam |
sāvadhānena manasā śrūyatāṃ tanmunīśvarāḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
caturthī koṭirudrasaṃhitā
4.32.d:
ततः परं च यज्जातं कुत्सितं कर्म दुःखदम् ।
सावधानेन मनसा श्रूयतां तन्मुनीश्वराः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
चतुर्थी कोटिरुद्रसंहिता
4.32.m:
Whatever vile, grief-causing deed took place after that— / let that be heard with an attentive mind, O best of sages!

Thus in the fourth book, the Koṭirudrasaṃhitā of the glorious Śivamahāpurāṇa, in the eulogy of Ghuśmeśvara, the thirty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Conduct of Sudehā and Sudharmā.'
